definition_zh: 敏感性；灵敏度；体贴；易受伤害的状态；（仪器）响应能力
definition_en: the quality of responding strongly to small changes, or of being easily hurt or moved

senses.title: The state of being easily affected
senses.titleCN: 易受影响的状态：一点变化就有反应
senses.definition: the quality of being readily affected by small changes or influences
senses.definitionCN: 容易被细微变化或影响所左右的性质
senses.example: The sensitivity of the instrument made the whole room a source of noise.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器的敏感度让整个房间都成了噪声源。
senses.why: Latin sentire 'to feel' gives sensus 'feeling'; the abstract noun -itas names the capacity to feel or be moved at all.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 sentire「感觉」产生 sensus「感觉」；抽象名词后缀 -itas 命名的是「能够感受或被触动」这一能力本身。

senses.title: Instrument responsiveness
senses.titleCN: 仪器灵敏度：最小可测变化
senses.definition: the smallest change a device can detect and report
senses.definitionCN: 装置能够察觉并报告的最小变化
senses.example: A higher sensitivity lets the detector find traces of lead.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的灵敏度让探测器能发现微量铅。
senses.why: Instruments were given the same word as nerves: both convert a faint input into a measurable output.
senses.whyCN: 仪器被赋予与神经相同的词：两者都把微弱的输入转换为可测量的输出。

senses.title: Easily hurt or offended
senses.titleCN: 易受伤、易被触怒：情绪上的薄皮
senses.definition: the tendency to be hurt or offended by small remarks or events
senses.definitionCN: 容易因细微言语或事件而受伤或被冒犯的倾向
senses.example: His sensitivity about his accent made meetings difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 他对口音的敏感让会议变得难开。
senses.why: The physical sense moved inward: what can be easily affected can also be easily wounded.
senses.whyCN: 物理义向内移动：容易被影响的东西，也容易受伤。

senses.title: Thoughtful awareness of others
senses.titleCN: 体贴周到：察觉他人的感受
senses.definition: careful awareness of other people's feelings and needs
senses.definitionCN: 对他人感受与需要的细心体察
senses.example: She handled the family's loss with great sensitivity.
senses.exampleCN: 她以极大的体贴处理了这个家庭的丧亲之痛。
senses.why: The same capacity turned outward becomes a virtue: to feel finely is also to notice what others feel.
senses.whyCN: 同一种能力转向他人便成了美德：感受得细腻，也就更能察觉他人所感。

senses.title: Medical sensitization
senses.titleCN: 医学上的敏感化：对某物反应过强
senses.definition: in medicine, an exaggerated response to a substance or stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指对某物质或刺激产生的过度反应
senses.example: Skin sensitivity to the ointment appeared after a week.
senses.exampleCN: 用药一周后出现了对该软膏的皮肤敏感。
senses.why: Clinical usage measures the threshold: a lowered threshold is named sensitivity, and the noun carries the diagnosis.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法测量阈值：阈值降低便被称为敏感，这个名词承载着诊断结论。

senses.title: Sensitivity in statistics
senses.titleCN: 统计敏感性：条件变化对结论的影响
senses.definition: the degree to which a result changes when assumptions or inputs change
senses.definitionCN: 当假设或输入改变时，结果随之改变的程度
senses.example: The sensitivity analysis showed the forecast depends on one price.
senses.exampleCN: 敏感性分析显示预测取决于一个价格。
senses.why: Modelling borrowed the word for 'easily affected': a model is sensitive when small inputs move its output.
senses.whyCN: 建模借用了「易受影响」这一含义：当微小输入能推动输出时，模型就是敏感的。

senses.title: Confidentiality needs
senses.titleCN: 保密敏感度：须谨慎处理的程度
senses.definition: the degree to which information must be handled with care
senses.definitionCN: 信息必须被谨慎处理的程度
senses.example: Documents of this sensitivity cannot leave the building.
senses.exampleCN: 这种敏感级别的文件不能带出大楼。
senses.why: From 'easily affected' comes 'easily damaged if mishandled', which is exactly what classified information is.
senses.whyCN: 从「易受影响」引出「处理不当便易受损」，而这正是机密信息的处境。

senses.title: Sensitivity to a market
senses.titleCN: 市场敏感度：对价格或需求的反应
senses.definition: in economics, the extent to which demand or price responds to a change
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中指需求或价格对某一变化的反应程度
senses.example: The sensitivity of demand to price rose during the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 短缺期间需求对价格的敏感度上升了。
senses.why: Economics uses the same measurement logic: how far does one variable move when another is nudged?
senses.whyCN: 经济学使用同样的测量逻辑：当一个变量被轻轻推动时，另一个变量会移动多远？

intro.en: Sensitivity joins the Latin verb sentire 'to feel' with the abstract suffix -itas, through the adjective sensitivus. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: sensitivity 经由形容词 sensitivus，把拉丁动词 sentire「感觉」与抽象后缀 -itas 结合起来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin sentire meant 'to feel, perceive, think'. Its noun sensus gave English sense, and the same verb underlies sensation, sentiment and consent.
items.cn: 拉丁 sentire 意为「感觉、察觉、思考」。其名词 sensus 产生英语 sense，同一动词也支撑 sensation、sentiment、consent。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed sensitivus 'capable of feeling', used for the faculty of sense in philosophy. The word named a capacity, not an instrument reading.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁构成 sensitivus「能够感觉的」，在哲学中用于指感官能力。这个词命名的是能力，而非仪器读数。

items.en: English sensitivity appears in the eighteenth century, first in physiology and philosophy, then in ordinary description of temperament. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 sensitivity 于 18 世纪出现，先用于生理学与哲学，随后用于对性情的日常描述。最早的确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Nineteenth-century photography and telegraphy needed a word for how faint a signal a material could register, and sensitivity moved into the laboratory.
items.cn: 19 世纪的摄影与电报需要为「材料能记录多弱的信号」找一个词，sensitivity 由此进入实验室。

items.en: Twentieth-century statistics and economics turned the word into a computed quantity: a sensitivity analysis asks how far an output moves when an input is nudged.
items.cn: 20 世纪的统计学与经济学把这个词变成可计算的量：敏感性分析问的是一个输入被轻推时，输出移动多远。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English date of sensitivity is uncertain; the deeper origin of sentire before its 'feel' sense is debated and any Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：sensitivity 的英语首见年代存疑；sentire 在「感觉」义之前的更深来源有争议，任何印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: The first group holds same-family nouns and adjectives that differ in part of speech or scope; the second holds near-synonyms for responsiveness.
note.cn: 第一组是同族名词与形容词，差别在词性或范围；第二组是表示响应能力的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a thing or person that responds readily; sensitivity is the noun naming that quality.
entries.definitionCN: 描述易于响应的事物或人；sensitivity 是命名该性质的名词。

entries.definition: Means refined emotional or aesthetic awareness. It shares sentire but names taste and feeling, not measurable response.
entries.definitionCN: 意为细腻的情感或审美感受力。它同出 sentire，但命名的是品味与情致，而非可测量的响应。

entries.definition: A physical feeling or a startling event. It is what is felt; sensitivity is the capacity to feel it.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体感觉或引起轰动的事件。它是被感受到的东西；sensitivity 是感受它的能力。

entries.definition: The instrument that detects a change. Sensitivity is its property; the sensor is the object that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 指探测变化的装置。sensitivity 是它的属性，sensor 是拥有该属性的物件。

entries.definition: The quality of reacting quickly to something. It is broader: a person, a market or a system can be responsive without being finely calibrated.
entries.definitionCN: 对事物迅速作出反应的性质。它更宽泛：人、市场或系统都可以有响应性，而不必精密校准。

entries.definition: The state of being likely to be harmed or influenced. It stresses weakness to attack, while sensitivity may be a useful precision.
entries.definitionCN: 容易受害或受影响的状况。它强调易受攻击的弱点，而 sensitivity 可能是一种有用的精度。

entries.definition: The ability to distinguish very small differences. Sensitivity is about detecting a faint signal; precision is about resolving close values.
entries.definitionCN: 分辨极小差异的能力。sensitivity 关乎察觉微弱信号，precision 关乎分辨接近的数值。

entries.definition: Conscious knowledge of a situation. It is cognitive, while sensitivity may be physical or emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 对处境的自觉认识。它属于认知层面，而 sensitivity 可能是生理或情绪层面的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sentire 'to feel' + -itas: the noun names the capacity to feel.
normal.cn: sentire「感觉」+ -itas：这个名词命名的是感受的能力。

normal.en: The family runs sense, sensation, sensitive, sensitivity, sensitize, sensor, sensory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sense、sensation、sensitive、sensitivity、sensitize、sensor、sensory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: sensitivity analysis, light sensitivity, cultural sensitivity, sensitivity to.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：敏感性分析、光敏度、文化敏感性、对……敏感。

normal.en: One word covers nerves, film, feelings and markets because all four convert a faint input into a response.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖神经、胶片、情绪与市场，因为这四者都把微弱输入转换为响应。

normal.en: sensitivity is the property; sensor is the device; sensation is what is felt.
normal.cn: sensitivity 是属性；sensor 是装置；sensation 是被感觉到的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a thin membrane that dents under a feather.
abstract.cn: 想象一片薄膜，一根羽毛就能让它凹陷。

abstract.en: Picture a needle that trembles before the wind is strong enough to feel.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针，在风还吹不动人时就已颤动。

abstract.en: Picture a person who hears the unsaid sentence in a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人能听见房间里那句没说出口的话。

examples.en: The sensitivity of the balance allows readings to a thousandth of a gram.
examples.cn: 这台天平的灵敏度可以读到千分之一克。

examples.en: Cultural sensitivity is essential when a clinic serves several communities.
examples.cn: 当一家诊所要服务多个社群时，文化敏感性必不可少。

examples.en: A sensitivity analysis showed that the conclusion held under every assumption tested.
examples.cn: 敏感性分析显示，在测试过的每种假设下结论都成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sense（感觉）+ itivity（能力）」——能感觉到细微变化的能力 → sensitivity 敏感性、灵敏度

root: 拉丁 sentire「感觉」→ sensus「感觉」→ sensitivus「能感觉的」→ 英语 sensitivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one capacity: something faintly touched responds strongly, and that capacity can belong to an instrument, a skin, a heart, a model or a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种能力展开：受到轻微触动的东西反应强烈，而这种能力可以属于仪器、皮肤、心、模型或市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin membrane that dents at the lightest touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄膜，最轻的触碰就能让它凹陷。

branches.en: CAPACITY ITSELF: the abstract property of being readily affected.
branches.cn: 能力本身：容易被影响这一抽象属性。

branches.en: MEASURED THRESHOLD: instruments and clinical tests quantify how faint a stimulus can be.
branches.cn: 可测阈值：仪器与临床检测量化刺激可以多微弱。

branches.en: INWARD AND OUTWARD: the same thin skin that is easily wounded also notices others' wounds.
branches.cn: 向内与向外：同一层薄皮既容易受伤，也能察觉他人的伤。

branches.en: SYSTEM RESPONSE: models and markets are sensitive when small inputs move outputs.
branches.cn: 系统响应：当微小输入推动输出时，模型与市场就是敏感的。

branches.en: HANDLING CARE: what is easily damaged must be treated with care.
branches.cn: 处置谨慎：容易受损的东西必须谨慎对待。

intro.en: Sensitivity is a Latin feeling verb plus a Latin abstract suffix, with no prefix.
intro.cn: sensitivity 是拉丁「感觉」动词加拉丁抽象后缀，没有前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire 'to feel' gives sensus and sensitivus; -itas turns the adjective into the abstract noun sensitivity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire「感觉」产生 sensus 与 sensitivus；-itas 把形容词转为抽象名词 sensitivity。

items.meaning: the quality of responding or being easily affected
items.meaningCN: 易于响应或易受影响的性质
items.example: Sensitivity varies with temperature.
items.exampleCN: 灵敏度随温度变化。

items.example: The skin is sensitive to sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 这种皮肤对阳光敏感。

items.example: The topic was handled sensitively.
items.exampleCN: 这个话题处理得很得体。

items.example: The plate was sensitized with silver salts.
items.exampleCN: 感光板用银盐做了敏化处理。

items.example: A sensor logged the humidity.
items.exampleCN: 传感器记录了湿度。

items.example: Sensory nerves carry the signal.
items.exampleCN: 感觉神经传递信号。

items.example: The word has two senses here.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在此有两个义项。

items.example: The remark was insensitive to her loss.

definition_en: to make an activity illegal and punishable by law
core_image: 议事厅里举起的手通过一条新条文，原本寻常的动作从此被写进罪名

senses.title: Make an act an offence
senses.titleCN: 立法把某行为定为犯罪
senses.definition: to place an activity under criminal law so that it can be punished
senses.definitionCN: 把某项活动纳入刑法范围，使其可受处罚
senses.example: Lawmakers voted to criminalize the sale of unlicensed medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 立法者投票把无证销售药品定为犯罪。
senses.why: Criminalize is criminal plus -ize 'to make': the verb makes a deed into a crime.
senses.whyCN: criminalize 是 criminal 加 -ize「使……成为」：这个动词把行为变成罪行。

senses.title: Turn lawful conduct unlawful
senses.titleCN: 使原本合法的事变为违法
senses.definition: to change the legal status of conduct that was previously permitted
senses.definitionCN: 改变原本被允许行为的法律地位
senses.example: The new rules criminalized what had been a routine practice for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 新规把几十年来的例行做法变成了违法行为。
senses.why: Making something criminal is the reverse of permitting it, and the suffix carries that reversal.
senses.whyCN: 把某事物定为犯罪，就是「允许」的反面，而这个词尾正承担这一翻转。

senses.title: Reach a category of people
senses.titleCN: 把某类人纳入刑事处罚范围
senses.definition: to bring a group of people within the reach of criminal penalties
senses.definitionCN: 使某一群体落入刑事处罚的适用范围
senses.example: Advocates argued that the measure criminalized the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 反对者主张这项措施把穷人推入刑事处罚范围。
senses.why: A law aimed at an act catches the people who habitually perform it, so the verb extends to them.
senses.whyCN: 针对行为的法律会网住在习惯性从事该行为的人，因此这个动词也扩展到人身上。

senses.title: Name an international crime
senses.titleCN: 在国际法层面定为罪行
senses.definition: to classify conduct as a crime under international law
senses.definitionCN: 依国际法把某行为归为罪行
senses.example: The statute criminalized the recruitment of child soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 该规约把征募儿童兵定为罪行。
senses.why: International tribunals apply the same verb to conduct that no single state can punish alone.
senses.whyCN: 国际法庭把同一个动词用于任何单个国家都无法独自惩处的行为。

senses.title: Treat as criminal in practice
senses.titleCN: 执法实践中事实上按犯罪处理
senses.definition: to treat conduct as criminal through enforcement even where the law is unclear
senses.definitionCN: 在法律不明晰时通过执法事实上按犯罪处理
senses.example: Critics said the police had criminalized homelessness by sweeping the camps.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说警方清理营地，事实上把无家可归者当作罪犯。
senses.why: Enforcement can do what a statute has not done, which is why the verb is used for de facto criminalization.
senses.whyCN: 执法可以做到法条尚未做到的事，因此这个动词也用于「事实上的入罪化」。

senses.title: Attach a penalty
senses.titleCN: 使某行为承受刑罚后果
senses.definition: to subject conduct to a penalty, fine or imprisonment
senses.definitionCN: 使某行为承受罚金、刑罚或监禁的后果
senses.example: The amendment criminalized late payment with a heavy fine.
senses.exampleCN: 修正案以重罚把逾期付款定为犯罪。
senses.why: A penalty is what makes a new offence real, so the verb is also used for the sanction itself.
senses.whyCN: 刑罚才让新罪名落到实处，因此这个动词也用于制裁本身。

senses.title: Make it an offence locally
senses.titleCN: 地方或行业规章层面的入罪化
senses.definition: to create an offence at the level of a local ordinance or a professional code
senses.definitionCN: 在市镇条例或行业规范层面新设罪名
senses.example: The city council criminalized camping in the station forecourt.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会把在车站前庭露营定为犯罪。
senses.why: Local bodies can create offences too, so the verb descends from statutes to ordinances.
senses.whyCN: 地方机构也能设罪名，因此这个动词从法条下降到条例。

senses.title: Be treated as a criminal
senses.titleCN: 被动用法：被当作罪犯对待
senses.definition: to be dealt with as a criminal, whether or not a charge follows
senses.definitionCN: 被按罪犯对待，无论随后是否提起指控
senses.example: Patients were criminalized for seeking help too often.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因求助过于频繁而被当作罪犯看待。
senses.why: The passive lets the verb describe an experience rather than a legislative act.
senses.whyCN: 被动式让这个动词可以描述一种经历，而不只是立法动作。

intro.en: Criminalize is an English verb from criminal plus the suffix -ize, which reaches English through French from Late Latin -izare and Greek -izein 'to make, to do'. It is recorded from the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: criminalize 是英语动词，由 criminal 加后缀 -ize 构成；-ize 经法语来自晚期拉丁 -izare，再上溯希腊 -izein「使、做」。这个词十九世纪起有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crimen 'charge, accusation' supplies the first part of criminal and hence of the verb.
items.cn: crimen「指控、控告」提供 criminal 的前半部分，也提供这个动词的前半部分。

items.en: Criminal named both the adjective and the person before the verb existed.
items.cn: 在动词出现之前，criminal 已兼指形容词与犯罪的人。

items.en: Greek -izein meant 'to make, to do'; Late Latin -izare and French -iser carried it into English as -ize.
items.cn: 希腊 -izein 意为「使、做」；晚期拉丁 -izare 与法语 -iser 把它带入英语，成为 -ize。

items.en: The verb appeared in legal and reforming writing, naming the act of putting conduct under criminal law.
items.cn: 这个动词出现在法律与改革写作中，指把行为纳入刑法的动作。

items.en: In the twentieth century it spread to debates about policing, morality and international tribunals.
items.cn: 二十世纪，它扩展到关于警务、道德与国际法庭的争论。

items.en: The chain criminal plus -ize is clear and the suffix has a documented history; only the earliest citation of the verb is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：criminal 加 -ize 的词源链清楚，后缀的历史也有记录，只有这个动词的最早书证没有确定年代。

note.en: Group one holds the crimen family, including the verb's direct relatives; group two holds verbs that restrain conduct by other means.
note.cn: 第一组是 crimen 词族，含这个动词的直接同族词；第二组是以其他手段限制行为的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective and the person; the verb differs by making something into an offence.
entries.definitionCN: 指形容词与犯罪的人；动词则多了「使某行为成为罪行」的意思。

entries.definition: The abstract state of being criminal, not the act of creating an offence.
entries.definitionCN: 指「属于犯罪」的抽象状态，而不是设置罪名的动作。

entries.definition: The academic study of crime, with no legislative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 研究犯罪的学科，不含立法含义。

entries.definition: De- 'away from' plus criminalize: to remove an offence from criminal law.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 criminalize：把某项罪名从刑法中移除。

entries.definition: To declare something illegal, often by decree; it stresses the ban more than the penalty.
entries.definitionCN: 宣布某事物非法，多带命令色彩，强调禁止甚于刑罚。

entries.definition: To forbid something officially; a ban may be administrative rather than criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁止某事，可能是行政禁令而非刑事罪名。

entries.definition: To forbid by law or rule, with no necessary link to prosecution.
entries.definitionCN: 依法或依规禁止，与是否起诉没有必然联系。

entries.definition: To impose a disadvantage or fine for conduct, which may stop short of a criminal charge.
entries.definitionCN: 对某行为施加不利后果或罚款，未必构成刑事指控。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Criminal plus -ize 'to make': making a deed into a crime.
normal.cn: criminal 加 -ize「使」：把行为做成罪行。

normal.en: The family runs criminal, criminality, criminalize, criminalization, decriminalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 criminal、criminality、criminalize、criminalization 与 decriminalize。

normal.en: Legislative verbs pair with it: vote to criminalize, move to criminalize.
normal.cn: 立法动词与它搭配：投票入罪、提议入罪。

normal.en: Its opposite is decriminalize, and the pair marks the two directions of a statute.
normal.cn: 它的反义动词是 decriminalize，这一对词标出法条的两种方向。

normal.en: The passive is common when the subject is a group of people rather than an act.
normal.cn: 当主语是一群人而不是某行为时，被动式更常见。

abstract.en: Picture a line being drawn on the ground where none was before.
abstract.cn: 想象在地上画出一条以前不存在的线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall, changing what counts as ordinary.
abstract.cn: 想象礼堂里举起一只手，改变了什么算寻常。

abstract.en: Picture a door that used to be open being quietly closed and locked.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇原本敞开的门被悄悄关上并上锁。

examples.cn: 该法规把持有未登记武器定为犯罪。

examples.en: Several cities have moved to criminalize sleeping in public spaces.
examples.cn: 若干城市已着手把在公共场所睡觉入罪。

examples.en: The tribunal criminalized the recruitment of children under fifteen.
examples.cn: 该法庭把征募十五岁以下儿童定为罪行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「criminal（罪犯）+ ize（使）」——使某事变成犯罪：入罪化

root: 英语 criminal（拉丁 criminalis，词根 crimen）+ 动词后缀 -ize（晚期拉丁 -izare，出自希腊 -izein「使、做」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one legislative act outward: a statute names an offence, changes a permitted practice, reaches a group, enters international law, is applied in the street, carries a penalty, appears in local rules and finally lands on the person treated as a criminal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次立法动作向外扩散：法条设定罪名、改变原本允许的做法、触及一个群体、进入国际法、在街头被执行、附带刑罚、出现在地方规则里，最后落到被当作罪犯的那个人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands raised in a chamber, a new clause on the screen, and an ordinary act turning into a charge.
core.cn: 核心意象：议事厅里举起的手，屏幕上一条新条文，一个寻常动作变成一项罪名。

branches.en: THE STATUTE: an activity is named and its legal status is reversed.
branches.cn: 法条：某项活动被点名，其法律地位被翻转。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE REACHED: penalties extend to a class of people, not only to a deed.
branches.cn: 被触及的人：刑罚延伸到一类人身上，而不只针对行为。

branches.en: ABOVE AND BELOW: international law names the crime, while patrols apply it in the street.
branches.cn: 上与下：国际法设定罪名，巡逻在街头执行。

branches.en: THE PENALTY AND THE PARISH: a fine attaches to the act, and a local ordinance creates the offence.
branches.cn: 刑罚与地方：罚金附着在行为上，地方条例也能新设罪名。

branches.en: THE PERSON AT THE END: the passive turns the verb into an experience of being treated as a criminal.
branches.cn: 最后落到人：被动式把这个动词变成「被当作罪犯」的经历。

intro.en: Criminalize is an English verb: a Latin-derived base plus a Greek-derived verb suffix.
intro.cn: criminalize 是英语动词：一个拉丁来源的词基，加一个希腊来源的动词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Crimen gives criminal; -izare, the Late Latin form of Greek -izein, gives the verb ending -ize and also builds organize, modernize and legalize.
latinIntro.cn: crimen 提供 criminal；希腊 -izein 的晚期拉丁形式 -izare 提供动词词尾 -ize，也构成 organize、modernize、legalize 等词。

senses.title: Imitate to entertain
senses.definition: to copy someone's voice, accent or mannerisms in order to amuse others
senses.definitionCN: 复制他人的嗓音、口音或举止以逗乐旁人
senses.example: He can mimic the lecturer so well that the class bursts out laughing.
senses.exampleCN: 他把讲师模仿得惟妙惟肖，全班都笑了出来。
senses.why: The verb keeps the oldest stage sense of mimos: a performer reproducing another's manner.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词保留了 mimos 最古老的舞台义：表演者复制他人的举止。

senses.title: Copy a model in order to learn
senses.definition: to reproduce an action or sound as a way of acquiring the skill
senses.definitionCN: 复制动作或声音，以此获得该项技能
senses.example: Children mimic the gestures of the adults around them long before they can name them.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们还叫不出这些动作的名称，就已经在模仿身边成人的手势。
senses.why: Copying is the cheapest learning device: the model supplies the pattern before the learner has a rule.
senses.whyCN: 复制是最省力的学习装置：学习者还没有规则时，范本先提供了样式。

senses.title: Imitate in order to deceive
senses.definition: to copy another's appearance or signals so that a observer draws a false conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 复制他者的外观或信号，使观察者得出错误判断
senses.example: Some spiders mimic ants to enter a colony unnoticed.
senses.exampleCN: 有些蜘蛛模仿蚂蚁，以便不被察觉地进入蚁巢。
senses.why: Deception is the dark twin of entertainment: both depend on the copy being accepted as the original.
senses.whyCN: 欺骗是娱乐的暗面双生：两者都依赖复制品被当作原件。

senses.title: Reproduce another system's behaviour
senses.titleCN: 复现另一系统的行为（仿真）
senses.definition: used of software, hardware or models that reproduce the behaviour of another system
senses.definitionCN: 用于软件、硬件或模型复现另一系统的行为
senses.example: The test rig mimics the vibration of a real wing.
senses.exampleCN: 试验台模拟真实机翼的振动。
senses.why: Engineering generalizes the biological sense: the copy needs to behave like the original, not look like it.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把生物义一般化：复制品需要行为像原件，而不必外形像。

senses.title: A person skilled at imitation
senses.definition: a person who can reproduce another's voice or manner convincingly
senses.definitionCN: 能令人信服地复现他人嗓音或举止的人
senses.example: She is the best mimic in the troupe.
senses.exampleCN: 她是剧团里最擅长模仿的人。
senses.why: The agent noun is simply the person who performs the act named by the verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个施动名词就是执行该动词所表行为的人。

senses.title: An organism resembling another species
senses.titleCN: 外形酷似另一物种的生物
senses.definition: an animal or plant that has evolved to look like another species
senses.definitionCN: 演化出与另一物种相似外形的动物或植物
senses.example: The hoverfly is a mimic of a wasp, but it has no sting.
senses.exampleCN: 这只食蚜蝇酷似黄蜂，却并没有蜇针。
senses.why: Biology turns the noun into a label for the copying organism itself.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把该名词转成对实施复制的生物本身的称呼。

senses.title: Attributive: imitative rather than genuine
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean that the thing imitates something else rather than being it
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示该物仿照他物而非其本身
senses.example: The fish has mimic colouring that copies a dead leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 这条鱼有模仿枯叶的体色。
senses.why: As an adjective the word moves from the actor to the feature that does the copying.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词从施动者转到实施复制的特征上。

senses.title: Of symptoms: resemble another disease
senses.definition: used of a condition whose signs copy those of a different disease, making diagnosis difficult
senses.definitionCN: 用于症状复制另一种疾病表现、使诊断困难的情形
senses.example: A benign cyst can mimic a tumour on a scan.
senses.exampleCN: 良性囊肿在扫描影像上可以酷似肿瘤。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the word for resemblance that misleads an expert observer, not a predator.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用这个词指误导专业观察者的相似，而非误导捕食者。

intro.en: Mimic reached English through French mimique from Latin mimicus, itself from Greek mimikos, an adjective of mimos 'imitator'. The adjective and noun are sixteenth-century, the verb seventeenth-century.
intro.cn: mimic 经法语 mimique 来自拉丁 mimicus，后者出自希腊 mimikos，即 mimos「模仿者」的形容词。形容词与名词见于 16 世纪，动词见于 17 世纪。

items.en: Greek mimos 'imitator, mime actor' is the base noun of the family.
items.cn: 希腊 mimos「模仿者、摹拟演员」是该词族的基础名词。

items.en: The Greek adjective mimikos 'imitative, of a mime' supplied the shape later taken by Latin mimicus.
items.cn: 希腊形容词 mimikos「模仿的、摹拟表演的」提供了后来拉丁 mimicus 所取的形态。

items.en: Latin mimicus is a borrowing of the Greek adjective; it is not an inherited Latin formation.
items.cn: 拉丁 mimicus 借自希腊形容词，并非拉丁语继承而来的构词。

items.en: French mimique carried the adjective into English, where mimic appeared as adjective and noun in the 1570s.
items.cn: 法语 mimique 把这个形容词带入英语，mimic 于 1570 年代作为形容词与名词出现。

items.en: The verb is generally dated to the 1680s, at first in the sense of burlesque imitation.
items.cn: 动词一般认为是 1680 年代出现，最初指滑稽模仿。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): Greek mimos is secure as the immediate source, but its own deeper origin is disputed and may be Pre-Greek; the 1570s and 1680s dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：希腊 mimos 作为直接来源是可靠的，但其更早的来源有争议，可能属前希腊语底层；1570 年代与 1680 年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same-family forms that are constantly swapped; group two holds verbs of copying that differ in purpose, fidelity or target.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中经常被混用的形式；第二组是复制类动词，区别在目的、逼真程度或对象。

entries.definition: The named phenomenon or practice; mimic is the actor or the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指被命名的现象或做法；mimic 指施动者或行为本身。

entries.definition: Describes something as imitative; mimic as an adjective is chiefly attributive and rarer.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物具有模仿性质；mimic 作形容词多作定语且更少见。

entries.definition: The past tense or participle, not the base verb; note the double k before -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式或过去分词，不是动词原形；注意 -ed 前双写 k。

entries.definition: A person who mimics; the formal agent noun, less common than the plain noun mimic.
entries.definitionCN: 指模仿的人；是正式的施动名词，不如直接用 mimic 常见。

entries.definition: The general verb for following a model; it lacks the playful or deceptive colour of mimic.
entries.definitionCN: 表示照着范本做的一般动词，没有 mimic 那种戏谑或欺骗色彩。

entries.definition: To copy a particular person's identity, usually for performance or fraud; mimic can take a voice or a species.
entries.definitionCN: 指复制某个特定人物的身份，多用于表演或行骗；mimic 的对象可以是嗓音或物种。

entries.definition: To copy clumsily or without understanding; it carries disapproval that mimic need not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 指笨拙或不加理解地照搬，含贬义，而 mimic 不一定含贬义。

entries.definition: To copy in order to equal or surpass; the goal is competition, not amusement or disguise.
entries.definitionCN: 指为达到或超越而仿效；目的是竞争，而非逗乐或伪装。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek-to-Latin route, the real inflected forms, and the collocations that distinguish the verb, noun and adjective uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊—拉丁路径、真实的屈折形式，以及区分动词、名词、形容词用法的固定搭配。

normal.en: mimos 'imitator' + -ic: belonging to an imitator.
normal.cn: mimos「模仿者」+ -ic：属于模仿者的。

normal.en: The family runs mimic, mimicry, mimetic, mimesis, mime.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mimic、mimicry、mimetic、mimesis、mime。

normal.en: Spelling note: mimics, mimicked, mimicking, with a doubled k.
normal.cn: 拼写要点：mimics、mimicked、mimicking，k 要双写。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mimic the accent, mimic the symptoms, a gifted mimic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 mimic the accent、mimic the symptoms、a gifted mimic。

normal.en: Three jobs: entertain, learn, deceive.
normal.cn: 三种功能：逗乐、学习、欺骗。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror that learns the face in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子学会了它前面的那张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a spy copying a doorman's walk to pass a checkpoint.
abstract.cn: 想象一名间谍复制门卫的步态以通过检查站。

abstract.en: Picture a machine rehearsing a wing's tremor until the numbers match.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器反复演练机翼的颤动，直到数据吻合。

examples.en: Parrots mimic household sounds with startling accuracy.
examples.cn: 鹦鹉能以惊人的准确度模仿家中的声音。

examples.en: The virus can mimic the body's own proteins and escape detection.
examples.cn: 这种病毒能模仿人体自身的蛋白以躲过识别。

examples.en: The robot was built to mimic a surgeon's hand movements.
examples.cn: 这台机器人被造来模拟外科医生的手部动作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mimi（模仿声）+ -ic」——会学样子的 → 模仿；模仿者

root: 希腊 mimos「模仿者」→ 希腊 mimikos「模仿的」→ 拉丁 mimicus（借自希腊语）→ 法语 mimique → 英语 mimic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses branch from one act of copying: entertain, learn, deceive, simulate a system, name the copier, name the resembling organism, describe the imitative feature, and describe a misleading symptom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一种复制行为分出：逗乐、学习、欺骗、模拟系统、称呼模仿者、称呼相似生物、描述仿制特征、描述误导性症状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person following another's voice and hands in a mirror, half a beat behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人对着镜子跟着另一个人的嗓音与手势，慢半拍。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE: a skilled copier reproduces a voice for an audience.
branches.cn: 表演：熟练的模仿者为观众复现嗓音。

branches.en: LEARNING: repetition installs the pattern in the learner.
branches.cn: 学习：重复把样式装进学习者。

branches.en: DECEPTION: animals, symptoms and signals pass as something they are not.
branches.cn: 欺骗：动物、症状与信号冒充成别的东西。

branches.en: SIMULATION: a system reproduces another system's behaviour.
branches.cn: 仿真：一个系统复现另一系统的行为。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTION: the word describes the feature that carries the copy.
branches.cn: 定语化：这个词描述承载复制特征的事物。

intro.en: Mimic is a Greek noun stem with an adjective ending, routed through Latin and French; the family supplies both verbs and abstract nouns.
intro.cn: mimic 是希腊语名词词干加形容词词尾，经拉丁语与法语传入；该词族既提供动词，也提供抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mimicus and mimus are Greek loans rather than native roots; they explain the shape of the French and English forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mimicus 与 mimus 是希腊语借词，而非本土词根；它们解释了法语与英语形式的由来。

items.example: Mimos named the stage imitator in Greek.
items.exampleCN: mimos 在希腊语中指舞台上的仿演者。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of a noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词词干变成形容词。

items.example: The child mimics the teacher.
items.exampleCN: 孩子模仿老师。

items.meaning: the practice or phenomenon of copying
items.example: Mimicry protects the hoverfly.
items.exampleCN: 拟态保护了这只食蚜蝇。

items.example: Mimetic art copies the visible world.
items.exampleCN: 模仿性艺术复制可见世界。

items.example: Mimesis was a key term in Greek criticism.
items.exampleCN: mimesis 是希腊文艺批评的关键术语。

items.example: He trained as a mime in Paris.
items.exampleCN: 他在巴黎学过哑剧。

items.example: A good mimicker hears the rhythm, not just the words.
items.exampleCN: 好的模仿者听的是节奏，而不只是词。

items.meaningCN: 作为行为研究的模仿动作
items.example: Mimicry behavior spreads through a flock.
items.exampleCN: 拟态行为会在鸟群中扩散。

latinEntries.structure: mimicus, mimica, mimicum (adjective, from Greek mimikos)

definition_zh: 寿命；使用寿命；存在期限；有效年限
definition_en: the length of time that a living thing, an object or a system lasts or is expected to last
core_image: 一支被刻上刻度的旧温度计，两端各有一道标记，中间拉出一条时间轴
scene: 博物馆的展柜里放着一支旧温度计，旁边的标签写着它从出厂到报废之间的年份跨度。 A simple label recorded the lifespan of the instrument from the day it was made to the day it failed.
sceneCN: 这里指器物从出厂到失效的使用寿命（第 4 个义项：产品与设备的使用期限）；句意为标签记下了这支仪器从制成到损坏的寿命。图中可辨识物件：展柜、旧温度计、刻度、纸质标签。

pos.zh: 名词：可数，指寿命或使用期限；常带表示所属的介词短语

derivatives.zh: 分写形式，与本词同义，多见于较早的文本
本词复数，指多个物种或多种产品的寿命
由 life 与 time 构成的近义复合词，义为「一生；终身」
由 life 与 long 构成，义为「终身的」
同一构词方式下的复合词，义为「翼展」
同一构词方式下的复合词，义为「时间跨度」

senses.title: Maximum lifespan of a species
senses.definition: the longest time that an individual of a species has been known to live under ideal conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种的个体在理想条件下已知能存活的最长时间
senses.example: The maximum lifespan of the bristlecone pine is measured in thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 刺果松的寿命上限以千年计。
senses.why: Biologists separate the ceiling from the average because the oldest known individual marks the genetic limit of a species.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家把上限与平均值分开，因为已知最老的个体标记着该物种的遗传极限。

senses.title: Average or expected lifespan
senses.definition: the typical number of years members of a group actually live, usually given as a mean
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体成员实际存活的典型年数，通常以平均值表示
senses.example: Average lifespan in the region rose by nearly a decade after clean water arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁水源到位后，该地区的平均寿命提高了近十年。
senses.why: Public health needs a single summary number, and the mean of many lives provides it.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要一个概括性的数字，众多个体寿命的平均值正好提供它。

senses.title: An individual's lifetime
senses.definition: the whole period during which one person or animal is alive
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一只动物活着的整个时期
senses.example: Her lifespan covered two wars and the first moon landing.
senses.exampleCN: 她的一生横跨两次战争与首次登月。
senses.why: The compound can also be read one life at a time, as a span with a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词也可以一次只指一条生命，看作有起点与终点的一段时间。

senses.title: Product or device lifespan
senses.titleCN: 产品与设备的使用寿命
senses.definition: the period for which a manufactured object remains usable before failure or replacement
senses.definitionCN: 制成品在失效或更换之前保持可用的时期
senses.example: The pump has a lifespan of about eight years under normal load.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵在正常负荷下的使用寿命约为八年。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the biological word because machines also wear out along a predictable curve.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了生物学的词，因为机器也沿着可预测的曲线磨损。

senses.title: Battery and component lifespan
senses.definition: the number of charge cycles or operating hours a component delivers before its capacity falls below a threshold
senses.definitionCN: 部件在容量降到阈值之前所能提供的充电循环次数或工作小时数
senses.example: Cycle testing is used to estimate the lifespan of the new cells.
senses.exampleCN: 循环测试被用来估算新电芯的寿命。
senses.why: A component's life is counted in cycles rather than years, so the word gains a technical unit.
senses.whyCN: 部件的寿命以循环而非年计数，这个词因此获得了技术性的计量单位。

senses.title: Lifespan of a star
senses.definition: the time a star spends fusing hydrogen and then heavier elements before it ends as a remnant
senses.definitionCN: 恒星从开始聚变氢到最终成为残骸所经历的时间
senses.example: A massive star has a much shorter lifespan than a small one.
senses.exampleCN: 大质量恒星的寿命远短于小质量恒星。
senses.why: Astronomy applies the same span to objects that were never alive, because their evolution has a clear start and finish.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把同一跨度用到了从未有生命的天体上，因为它们的演化有明确的开始与结束。

senses.title: Lifespan of an institution or custom
senses.definition: the period during which an organisation, language or practice continues to exist
senses.definitionCN: 组织、语言或习俗持续存在的时期
senses.example: The guild had a lifespan of three centuries before it dissolved.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行会存在了三个世纪才解散。
senses.why: Social scientists extend the word to anything that is founded, maintained and finally ended.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学家把这个词扩展到任何被创立、维持并最终结束的事物。

senses.title: Lifespan of stored data
senses.titleCN: 数据与载体的保存寿命
senses.definition: the time for which a storage medium keeps its contents readable without error
senses.definitionCN: 存储介质在不出现错误的情况下保持内容可读的时间
senses.example: Archivists test the lifespan of optical discs before committing to them.
senses.exampleCN: 档案人员在使用光盘之前会测试其保存寿命。
senses.why: Digital preservation turned the word into a specification: how long before the bits decay.
senses.whyCN: 数字保存把这个词变成了一项指标：比特在多长时间后开始劣化。

senses.title: Working lifespan
senses.titleCN: 职业寿命与有效工作年限
senses.definition: the number of years a person can remain in a demanding job or profession
senses.definitionCN: 一个人能留在高强度岗位或专业领域工作的年数
senses.example: Better recovery routines have extended the working lifespan of many athletes.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的恢复安排延长了许多运动员的职业寿命。
senses.why: Careers also begin, peak and end, so the biological span is applied to employment.
senses.whyCN: 职业生涯同样有开始、顶峰与结束，于是生物学的跨度被用到就业上。

intro.en: The word is a plain English compound of life and span, whose second element first meant the distance from thumb to little finger. The source is clear; the date of the compound's first recorded use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是 life 与 span 组成的普通英语复合词，其中 span 最初指拇指到小指之间的一拃长度。来源清楚，复合词的确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Spann named a unit of length, the stretch between an outstretched thumb and the little finger.
items.cn: 这个词原是一个长度单位，指张开拇指与小指之间的一拃。

items.en: From a hand's width the sense widened to any stretch or extent, and then to a stretch of time.
items.cn: 从一只手的宽度，词义扩展到任何伸展或范围，再扩展到一段时间。

items.en: Life has meant a living being's existence since the oldest English records.
items.cn: 自最早的英语文献起，这个词就指活物的存在。

items.en: Life and span joined to name the length of one life, first recorded in American usage in the mid-nineteenth century.
items.cn: 两者结合，用来指一条生命的长度，最早见于十九世纪中期的美国用法。

items.en: The compound then spread from creatures to machines, batteries, stars and institutions.
items.cn: 此后这个复合词从生物扩展到机器、电池、恒星与机构。

items.en: Reference works differ by decades on the earliest citation, so the first date is best given as approximate.
items.cn: 各类辞书对最早引例的年份相差数十年，因此首见年代只能给约数。

note.en: The first group shares the second element or the same compound pattern; the second group names other measures of duration.
note.cn: 第一组共享第二个构词成分或相同的复合方式；第二组表示其他「时长」概念。

entries.definition: The two-word spelling of the same compound.
entries.definitionCN: 同一复合词的分写形式。

entries.definition: The distance from one wing tip to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一侧翼尖到另一侧翼尖的距离。

entries.definition: A period of time between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 两个时点之间的一段时间。

entries.definition: How long a person can concentrate on one task.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人能专注于一项任务的时间长度。

entries.definition: The whole period during which someone is alive.
entries.definitionCN: 某人活着的整个时期。

entries.definition: The number of years a person is statistically expected to live.
entries.definitionCN: 按统计预期一个人能活的年数。

entries.definition: Long duration of life, especially an unusually long one.
entries.definitionCN: 长寿，尤指异常长的寿命。

entries.definition: The length of time during which something continues.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物持续的时长。

entries.definition: The period an object remains usable in service.
entries.definitionCN: 物体在使用中保持可用的期限。

entries.definition: The time food or a product stays good before spoiling.
entries.definitionCN: 食品或产品在变质前保持良好状态的时间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations run from the hand-span measure to a life, then to machines and stars; abstract ones treat the word as a bounded interval.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想从「一拃」的量度走到一条生命，再到机器与恒星；抽象联想把这个词看作一段有界的区间。

normal.en: Span first meant a hand's width, thumb to little finger.
normal.cn: 表示跨度的那个成分最初指一只手的宽度，从拇指到小指。

normal.en: Stretch the hand into a timeline and you get a life span.
normal.cn: 把手张开拉成一条时间轴，就得到了生命周期。

normal.en: A pump outlives its warranty but still has a lifespan.
normal.cn: 泵的保修期早过了，但它仍有使用寿命。

normal.en: A battery counts its life in cycles, not birthdays.
normal.cn: 电池的寿命以循环计，而不是以生日计。

normal.en: Stars are not alive, yet they too have a lifespan.
normal.cn: 恒星没有生命，却同样有寿命。

abstract.en: A lifespan is not a number but an interval with two edges.
abstract.cn: 寿命不是一个数字，而是一段有两条边的区间。

abstract.en: Anything founded can also be spent, which is why institutions borrow the word.
abstract.cn: 凡被创立者皆可耗尽，机构因此也借用这个词。

abstract.en: Knowing the span changes how you plan the middle of it.
abstract.cn: 知道跨度有多长，会改变你对中间那段日子的安排。

examples.en: The average lifespan of the species is about twelve years.
examples.cn: 该物种的平均寿命约为十二年。

examples.en: Regular maintenance can double the lifespan of the machine.
examples.cn: 定期维护能让这台机器的寿命翻倍。

examples.en: Researchers compared the lifespan of wild and captive animals.
examples.cn: 研究人员比较了野生与圈养动物的寿命。

dict_mnemonic.text: life（生命）+ span（跨度）——生命的跨度就是寿命

root: 由英语 life「生命」与 span「跨度」复合而成。span 源自古英语 spann，本指拇指到小指张开的一拃长度，后引申为任何延伸范围与时间跨度。复合词最早见于十九世纪中期的美国用法，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses extend one measure of duration from a species to a single life, then to pumps, batteries, stars, guilds and archives.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把同一个「时长」量度从物种延伸到单个生命，再到泵、电池、恒星、行会与档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid along a life, with a mark at each end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子贴着一条生命摆放，两端各有一道刻痕。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGICAL RANGE: the ceiling a species can reach and the average its members actually reach.
branches.cn: 生物学区间：物种能达到的上限与成员实际达到的平均值。

branches.en: THE SINGLE SPAN: one person's whole stretch of being alive.
branches.cn: 单条跨度：一个人活着的整段时光。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERED SPAN: a product's usable years and a component's counted cycles.
branches.cn: 工程跨度：产品的可用年数与部件的循环计数。

branches.en: THE NON-LIVING SPAN: a star's fusion years and a disc's readable years.
branches.cn: 非生命跨度：恒星的聚变年数与光盘的可读年数。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL SPAN: how long an institution lasts and how long a career lasts.
branches.cn: 社会跨度：机构能存续多久，职业能维持多久。

intro.en: The word is an English compound rather than a prefixed form, so its parts are two free morphemes.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语复合词而非前缀派生形式，因此它的组成部分是两个自由语素。

latinIntro.en: Its second element goes back to an Old English measure of length; the first is the ordinary word for being alive.
latinIntro.cn: 第二个成分可追溯到古英语的长度量度；第一个成分就是表示「活着」的常用词。

items.example: It is the first element and the oldest word for being alive.
items.exampleCN: 它是第一个成分，也是表示活着的最古老词。

items.example: The word began as a body-based unit of length.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初是以身体为依据的长度单位。

items.example: Its meaning widened from width to duration.
items.exampleCN: 它的词义从宽度扩展到了时长。

items.example: The compound is the base form used in this entry.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是本词条的基本形式。

items.example: It shows the same span pattern applied to wings.
items.exampleCN: 它展示了同一构词方式用在翅膀上。

items.example: It applies the pattern to time itself.
items.exampleCN: 它把这一方式用到时间本身。

items.example: The pattern extends to mental endurance.
items.exampleCN: 这一方式延伸到心理耐力。

items.example: A near-synonym built from the same first element.
items.exampleCN: 由同一第一个成分构成的近义词。

items.example: The adjective shows the first element in another compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词展示了第一个成分的另一复合用法。

derivatives.zh: 分写形式，与本词同义，多见于较早的文本
本词复数，指多个物种或多种产品的寿命
由 life 与 time 构成的近义复合词，义为「一生；终身」
由 life 与 long 构成，义为「终身的」
同一构词方式下的复合词，义为「翼展」
同一构词方式下的复合词，义为「时间跨度」

definition_zh: 定量分析；数量分析；以测量数值与统计方法研究问题；化学中测定成分含量；量化评估与建模
definition_en: the study of a question by measuring quantities and working with numerical data, including statistical, chemical and economic forms
core_image: 天平读数落进表格，一列数字被画成曲线，结论从曲线里长出来
scene: 实验室把水样分成十二份，逐份称重、记录浓度，再把数字画成曲线。 The team ran a quantitative analysis of the river samples before the dam was approved.
sceneCN: 这里指用测量数值研究样本（第 1 个义项：以测量数值为基础的分析）；句意为在大坝获批之前，团队对河水样本做了一次定量分析。场景要点：分装的水样、天平、记录表、逐点连成的浓度曲线。

pos.zh: 定量分析；数量分析

derivatives.zh: 由修饰形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「定量地、就数量而言」
由同一拉丁词干构成动词，义为「量化、用数量表示」
由量化动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「量化」
由同一拉丁词根构成名词，义为「数量」
由该短语缩合而成的职业称谓，义为「量化分析师」

senses.title: Analysis built on measured numbers
senses.titleCN: 以测量数值为基础的分析
senses.definition: the study of a question by measuring quantities and reasoning from numerical data rather than impressions
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量数量、依据数值数据推理来研究问题，而不是凭印象判断
senses.example: The lab ran a quantitative analysis of the soil before the field was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地出售之前，实验室对土壤做了一次定量分析。
senses.why: Quantus in Latin asks how much, so the first thing this analysis does is put a number on its object.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quantus 问的是「多少」，因此这种分析做的第一件事就是给对象配上一个数字。

senses.title: The statistical procedure itself
senses.definition: the set of statistical operations, such as sampling, regression and significance testing, applied to a body of data
senses.definitionCN: 对一组数据施行的一整套统计操作，如抽样、回归与显著性检验
senses.example: Their quantitative analysis used a regression model on ten years of shipping records.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的定量分析对十年的航运记录使用了回归模型。
senses.why: Once data are numbers, the methods that compare them become part of the phrase, not a separate step.
senses.whyCN: 数据一旦成为数字，比较这些数字的方法也就并入这个短语，而不再是一道单独的工序。

senses.title: Chemical determination of amounts
senses.definition: the branch of chemistry that establishes how much of each substance a sample contains
senses.definitionCN: 化学中测定样本含多少某种物质的分支
senses.example: Quantitative analysis showed 0.3 milligrams of lead per litre of water.
senses.exampleCN: 定量分析显示每升水含零点三毫克铅。
senses.why: Chemistry split the phrase in two: qualitative work says what is present, quantitative work says how much.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个短语一分为二：定性工作说明有什么，定量工作说明有多少。

senses.title: Measurement of performance or risk
senses.titleCN: 绩效与风险的量化评估
senses.definition: the conversion of performance, cost or risk into indicators that can be compared and tracked
senses.definitionCN: 把绩效、成本或风险换算成可以比较与追踪的指标
senses.example: A quantitative analysis of accident risk guided the new speed limit.
senses.exampleCN: 对事故风险的量化评估为新的限速规定提供了依据。
senses.why: Risk, cost and performance have no common scale until they are rated, and rating is exactly what the quantitative half does.
senses.whyCN: 风险、成本与绩效本来没有共同尺度，只有打分才有，而这正是「定量」那一半做的事。

senses.title: The numerical section of a report
senses.definition: the part of a study or report that carries figures, tables and calculations, as distinct from discussion
senses.definitionCN: 研究报告里承载数字、表格与计算的部分，与讨论部分相区别
senses.example: The quantitative analysis fills the first half of the report; the interviews come later.
senses.exampleCN: 定量分析占了报告的前一半，访谈材料放在后面。
senses.why: A report is divided by what it contains, and the half made of numbers borrows the name of the method.
senses.whyCN: 报告按内容划分，由数字构成的那一半就借用了方法的名称。

senses.title: Analysis of amount rather than kind
senses.titleCN: 只问多少、不问性质的分析
senses.definition: the contrastive use of the phrase when it is set against qualitative work that describes qualities and reasons
senses.definitionCN: 与描述性质与原因的定性研究相对照时的用法
senses.example: Where qualitative work asks why, quantitative analysis asks how many and how much.
senses.exampleCN: 定性研究问的是为什么，定量分析问的是多少。
senses.why: The adjective carries the contrast inside it: quantity on one side, quality on the other.
senses.whyCN: 形容词本身就把对照装了进来：一边是数量，另一边是性质。

senses.title: Economic and financial modelling
senses.definition: the use of mathematical models and market data to estimate returns, prices or policy effects
senses.definitionCN: 用数学模型与市场数据估算收益、价格或政策效果
senses.example: The bank's quantitative analysis projected a small fall in demand next quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 该银行的定量分析预计下季度需求会小幅下降。
senses.why: Finance took the statistical half of the phrase and made it a modelling practice with its own tools.
senses.whyCN: 金融业取走了这个短语中统计的那一半，把它做成了一门有专门工具的建模实践。

senses.title: Quantified comparison across cases
senses.definition: the comparison of groups, sites or periods by turning their features into figures on one scale
senses.definitionCN: 把不同群体、地点或时期的特征换算到同一尺度上再作比较
senses.example: A quantitative analysis across forty schools ranked them by attendance and spending.
senses.exampleCN: 对四十所学校做的定量分析按出勤率与经费把它们排出次序。
senses.why: Comparison needs a common unit, and measuring supplies one, so the phrase covers ranking as well as describing.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要共同单位，测量正好提供单位，因此这个短语既指描述也指排序。

senses.title: Data-based assessment before a decision
senses.definition: the practical use of numerical evidence to support or block a decision
senses.definitionCN: 用数值证据支持或阻止一项决定的实际用法
senses.example: The board asked for a quantitative analysis before approving the new line.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会要求先做定量分析，再批准新的生产线。
senses.why: A decision needs one common measure to weigh alternatives, so numerical evidence takes the phrase's name in boardrooms.
senses.whyCN: 决定需要一种共同尺度来衡量各种选择，因此在会议室里，数值证据就用了这个短语的名字。

intro.en: Quantitative comes from Latin quantus, how much, through the medieval adjective quantitativus; analysis comes from Greek analysis, a loosening up, built on ana- up and lysis a loosening. English joined the two in the nineteenth century for work that measures rather than describes.
intro.cn: quantitative 来自拉丁语 quantus「多少」，经中世纪拉丁语形容词 quantitativus 而来；analysis 来自希腊语 analysis「解开」，由 ana-「向上、彻底」与 lysis「松开」构成。英语在十九世纪把两者合起来，指以测量而非描述为主的工作。

items.en: Quantus asked how much or how great, and it stands behind the whole English family of quantity words.
items.cn: 这个词问的是「多少、多大」，英语里整族「数量」词都由它而来。

items.en: Schoolmen formed the adjective to mean concerned with amount, giving the phrase its first half.
items.cn: 中世纪的学者造出这个形容词，意为「与数量有关的」，为这个短语提供了前半。

items.en: Analysis named a loosening up, and Greek geometry used it for resolving a problem into its parts.
items.cn: analysis 本指「松开」，希腊几何学用它表示把问题拆解成各个部分。

items.en: The two words were joined in English scientific writing; the first use of the full phrase is uncertain and is usually dated only to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 这两个词在英语科学写作中合成短语；该完整短语的首次使用年代不确定，通常只笼统归到十九世纪。

items.en: The phrase became the name of the chemical branch that determines how much of a substance a sample holds.
items.cn: 这个短语成为化学分支的名称，专门测定样本含有多少某物质。

items.en: Sampling, regression and modelling widened it to any numerical study of data, and finance gave it a modelling trade.
items.cn: 抽样、回归与建模把它扩展到一切针对数据的数值研究，金融业又给了它一门建模行当。

note.en: The first group shares the measuring vocabulary; the second names the neighbouring kinds of study.
note.cn: 第一组共享「测量」这套词汇；第二组是与它相邻的各种研究名目。

entries.definition: The adverb of the same adjective, meaning in terms of amount.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词变来的副词，指「就数量而言」。

entries.definition: The verb for turning something into measurable amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事物换算成可测量的数量。

entries.definition: The noun for an amount or number of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物的数量。

entries.definition: Study of what a substance or case is like rather than how much of it there is.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质或案例的性质，而不是数量。

entries.definition: The act of breaking a problem into its parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指把问题拆成各个部分的行为。

entries.definition: Analysis that applies probability and sampling methods to data.
entries.definitionCN: 对数据运用概率与抽样方法的分析。

entries.definition: The act of establishing size, amount or degree with an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 用仪器确定大小、数量或程度。

entries.definition: The general term for examining collected figures, of which the quantitative kind is one form.
entries.definitionCN: 检查所收集数字的泛称，定量分析是其中一种形式。

entries.definition: A judgement of value, risk or performance, often using numbers but not always.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值、风险或表现的判断，常用数字但不限于数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin question behind the word, its real family and its real laboratory phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的拉丁提问、真实同族词与真实实验室说法。

normal.en: Quantus is Latin for how much, so quantitative work always answers a how-much question.
normal.cn: quantus 在拉丁语里是「多少」，所以定量工作回答的永远是「多少」的问题。

normal.en: Quantity, quantify and quantitative share one stem: if you can count it, the family fits.
normal.cn: 数量、量化与定量的词干相同：只要能数，就归这一族。

normal.en: Analysis in Greek is a loosening, so quantitative analysis loosens a problem into numbers.
normal.cn: analysis 在希腊语里是「松开」，定量分析就是把问题拆成数字。

normal.en: Chemical quantitative analysis asks how much lead is in the water, not what is in it.
normal.cn: 化学定量分析问的是水里有多少铅，而不是水里有什么。

normal.en: The phrase is two words doing two jobs: the adjective names the kind, the noun names the work.
normal.cn: 这个短语是两个词各干一件事：形容词说明种类，名词说明工作。

abstract.en: A number is a description that has agreed to be compared with other descriptions.
abstract.cn: 数字是一种答应与别的描述相比较的描述。

abstract.en: Measuring turns an argument about impressions into an argument about figures.
abstract.cn: 测量把关于印象的争论变成关于数字的争论。

abstract.en: Every quantitative claim leaves something unmeasured, and the skill lies in knowing what was left out.
abstract.cn: 每一个定量结论都留下了未被测量的东西，功夫就在知道漏掉了什么。

examples.en: The report opens with a quantitative analysis of traffic flow at the junction.
examples.cn: 报告以对路口车流量的定量分析开篇。

examples.en: Quantitative analysis of the alloy found less than one per cent nickel.
examples.cn: 对该合金的定量分析发现镍含量不到百分之一。

examples.en: Before the merger, the bank commissioned a quantitative analysis of credit risk.
examples.cn: 合并之前，这家银行委托做了一次信用风险的定量分析。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「框提忒提夫 分析」——先把东西框起来称一称，再拆开来看：定量分析

root: 拉丁语 quantus「多少」→ 中世纪拉丁语 quantitativus「与数量有关的」＋希腊语 analysis「解开、拆解」（ana-「彻底」＋lysis「松开」）；完整短语的英语首见年代不确定，通常列在十九世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses divide the phrase by what it is applied to: a measured sample, the statistical machinery, chemical amounts, risk and performance, the numerical half of a report, the contrast with qualitative work, market modelling, cross-case comparison, and support for a decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项按适用对象分开：被测样本、统计方法、化学含量、风险与绩效、报告中的数字部分、与定性工作的对照、市场建模、跨案例比较、以及为决策提供依据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance reading is written into a table, and a curve grows out of the numbers.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平读数被写进表格，一条曲线从这些数字里长出来。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SAMPLE: a question about amount answered from readings.
branches.cn: 被测样本：一个关于多少的问题，用读数来回答。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND ITS MIRROR: statistical operations on one side, the contrast with qualitative work on the other.
branches.cn: 方法与其镜像：一边是统计操作，另一边是与定性工作的对照。

branches.en: THE CHEMICAL AMOUNT: how much of a substance a sample holds.
branches.cn: 化学含量：一份样本里含有多少某物质。

branches.en: THE QUANTIFIED JUDGEMENT AND THE PAPER: risk and performance rated, a market modelled, a report's numerical half.
branches.cn: 量化判断与纸面：风险与绩效被打分，市场被建模，报告的数字部分成形。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON AND THE CHOICE: cases ranked on one scale, a decision carried by figures.
branches.cn: 比较与抉择：案例被排在同一尺度上，决定由数字来支撑。

intro.en: The entry is a compound of a Latin adjective and a Greek noun, and each half brings its own endings and family.
intro.cn: 这条词目是一个拉丁形容词与一个希腊名词的复合，两半各带自己的词尾与词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies quantus and quantitas, and the medieval adjective quantitativus is a schoolroom formation on the same stem; Greek supplies analysis and lysis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 quantus 与 quantitas，中世纪的 quantitativus 是在同一词干上的学堂造词；希腊语提供了 analysis 与 lysis。

items.example: The word asks for an amount, not a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词问的是数量，不是性质。

items.example: The noun names the thing the question asks for.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指提问所要的那个东西。

items.example: The adjective was coined in the schools to label this kind of work.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在学堂里被造出来，用来标记这一类工作。

items.meaning: a loosening, a resolution into parts
items.example: Geometry used it for taking a problem apart.
items.exampleCN: 几何学用它表示把问题拆开。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of going right through.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加进「一路贯穿」的意思。

items.example: The noun supplies the picture of something coming undone.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「东西被解开」的画面。

items.example: It turns the noun of amount into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把表示数量的名词变成形容词。

items.example: It gives the adverb for measuring something.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「以测量方式」的副词。

items.example: The verb names the act of putting a number on something.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指给某物配上数字的动作。

derivatives.zh: 由修饰形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「定量地」
由同一词干构成动词，义为「量化」
由量化动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「量化」
由同一拉丁词根构成名词，义为「数量」
由该短语缩合而成的职业称谓，义为「量化分析师」

definition_zh: 碳足迹（某一活动、产品、个人或机构直接与间接产生的温室气体排放总量，通常以二氧化碳当量计）
definition_en: the total greenhouse gases released directly and indirectly by an activity, product, person or organisation, usually expressed as carbon dioxide equivalent
core_image: 一双脚印从油田、货轮、工厂一路踩到餐盘，每一处都留下看不见的气体，最后合成一个数字
scene: 学生算出一顿午餐从种植、运输到烹饪的全部排放。 The carbon footprint of the conference included every flight the speakers took.
sceneCN: 这里 carbon footprint 指「某项活动全链条排放的总量」（第 2 个义项：活动或事件的排放总量）；句意为这场会议的碳足迹包括了每位讲者的每一段飞行。

pos.zh: 碳足迹（可数名词短语，复数直接加 -s；加不定冠词指一个具体总量）

derivatives.zh: foot（古英语 fōt）+ print（古法语 preinte「印记」，源自拉丁 premere「压」）→ 脚印；影响范围
拉丁 carbo（木炭）→ 碳：以炭命名的元素
eco-（希腊 oikos「家宅」）+ logical + footprint → 生态足迹：人类占用土地与水面的面积
water + footprint → 水足迹：一项活动耗用的水量
e-（向外）+ mittere（拉丁「送出」）+ -ion → 排放：向外释出的气体或物质
off（离开）+ set（放置）→ 抵消：用另一处的减排补上这里的排放

senses.title: The attributed total
senses.titleCN: 归到某对象头上的排放总量
senses.definition: the sum of greenhouse gases attributed to a defined object, whether a person, product or institution
senses.definitionCN: 归到某个确定对象名下的温室气体总和，对象可以是人、产品或机构
senses.example: Every organisation now publishes an annual carbon footprint.
senses.exampleCN: 如今每个机构都会公布年度碳足迹。
senses.why: the phrase works by attaching an invisible quantity to something you can point at.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语的做法是把一个看不见的量挂到你能指认的对象上。

senses.title: An event's total
senses.titleCN: 活动或事件的排放总量
senses.definition: the emissions of a gathering, trip or project, including travel, energy and waste
senses.definitionCN: 一次集会、旅程或项目的排放，包含交通、能源与废物
senses.example: The carbon footprint of the conference included every flight the speakers took.
senses.exampleCN: 这场会议的碳足迹包括了每位讲者的每一段飞行。
senses.why: a one-off event has no fixed plant to measure, so the accounting follows people and services.
senses.whyCN: 一次性活动没有固定厂房可量，核算只能跟着人与服务走。

senses.title: A product's life cycle
senses.definition: emissions from extracting materials, manufacturing, shipping, use and disposal of a good
senses.definitionCN: 一件商品从取料、制造、运输、使用到处置的排放
senses.example: The carbon footprint of a beef burger is dominated by land use.
senses.exampleCN: 一个牛肉汉堡的碳足迹主要来自土地利用。
senses.why: a product touches many processes, so its footprint is assembled from every stage of its life.
senses.whyCN: 一件产品牵涉许多过程，其足迹由生命的每个阶段拼成。

senses.title: The personal account
senses.definition: the emissions a household causes through heating, travel, food and goods
senses.definitionCN: 家庭因取暖、出行、饮食与购物造成的排放
senses.example: Flying less is the fastest way to shrink a personal carbon footprint.
senses.exampleCN: 少坐飞机是缩小个人碳足迹最快的办法。
senses.why: the phrase became popular because it turns a global problem into a number one person can act on.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语流行起来，是因为它把全球问题变成了一个人可以行动的数字。

senses.title: A measurement standard
senses.definition: the accounting convention that converts methane, nitrous oxide and other gases into carbon dioxide equivalent
senses.definitionCN: 把甲烷、氧化亚氮等气体折算成二氧化碳当量的核算口径
senses.example: The carbon footprint is reported in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent.
senses.exampleCN: 碳足迹以二氧化碳当量的吨数报告。
senses.why: different gases warm differently, so one common unit is needed before anything can be added up.
senses.whyCN: 不同气体的升温能力不同，必须先有共同单位才能相加。

senses.title: A label and a claim
senses.definition: a figure printed on packaging or advertising to inform buyers
senses.definitionCN: 印在包装或广告上供消费者参考的数字
senses.example: The carbon footprint on the packet lets shoppers compare brands.
senses.exampleCN: 包装上的碳足迹让购物者可以比较品牌。
senses.why: once measured, the number becomes a communication device as much as a scientific one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被测量，这个数字就既是科学工具也是传播工具。

senses.title: Offsetting and neutrality
senses.definition: the use of purchased credits to claim that a footprint has been cancelled
senses.definitionCN: 用购买的信用声称足迹已被抵消
senses.example: A carbon footprint can be offset on paper without any real reduction.
senses.exampleCN: 碳足迹可以在纸面上被抵消，而实际排放毫无减少。
senses.why: the accounting unit invites a market answer, and the market answer can diverge from the physical one.
senses.whyCN: 这个核算单位招来了市场式答案，而市场答案可能与物理事实脱节。

senses.title: National and corporate inventories
senses.definition: the aggregate figure used in reporting, regulation and supply-chain management
senses.definitionCN: 用于报告、监管与供应链管理的汇总数字
senses.example: Governments compare their carbon footprint with their stated targets.
senses.exampleCN: 各国政府把本国碳足迹与既定目标相比较。
senses.why: the same arithmetic scales from a household to a state, which is why the phrase travels so far.
senses.whyCN: 同一套算法能从家庭放大到国家，这正是这个短语传播如此之广的原因。

senses.title: The critical view
senses.titleCN: 批判视角：个体化与误差
senses.definition: the objection that personal footprints shift blame from industry and hide large uncertainties
senses.definitionCN: 认为个人足迹把责任从工业转给个人并掩盖巨大不确定性的批评
senses.example: Critics call the carbon footprint a convenient way to blame shoppers.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称碳足迹是一种方便地把责任推给购物者的办法。
senses.why: a measure that is easy to personalise is also easy to use as a distraction.
senses.whyCN: 一个容易个人化的指标，也容易被用来转移注意力。

intro.en: Carbon footprint joins the Latin-derived element name with a compound of Old English foot and Old French print, from Latin premere 'to press'. The phrase is a late twentieth-century extension of ecological footprint, which was coined in the early 1990s; the carbon version spread in the 2000s.
intro.cn: carbon footprint 把拉丁语源的元素名，接在古英语 foot 与古法语 print（源自拉丁 premere「压」）构成的复合词上。这个短语是二十世纪后期对生态足迹的延伸；生态足迹造于一九九〇年代初，碳版本在二〇〇〇年代流行。

items.en: Fōt meant the foot and also the track it leaves, a sense present from the earliest records.
items.cn: fōt 指脚，也指脚留下的痕迹，这个含义自最早文献就有。

items.en: Premere 'to press' produced Old French preinte 'impression', the source of English print.
items.cn: premere「压」产生古法语 preinte「印痕」，是英语 print 的来源。

items.en: Footprint first meant the mark of a foot, and only later the area a building or activity occupies.
items.cn: footprint 最初指脚的印记，后来才指建筑或活动占用的面积。

items.en: Lavoisier's circle fixed carbone as the element's name; English took it as carbon.
items.cn: 拉瓦锡一派把 carbone 定为该元素之名；英语取用为 carbon。

items.en: Wackernagel and Rees coined ecological footprint for the land area needed to support consumption.
items.cn: 瓦克纳格尔与里斯造出 ecological footprint，指支撑消费所需的土地面积。

items.en: Companies and campaigners turned the metaphor into a carbon-specific figure, and advertising fixed the phrase.
items.cn: 企业与倡导者把这个比喻改造成以碳为单位的数字，广告使这个短语固定下来。

note.en: Group one holds the sibling footprint and carbon-claim terms most often swapped in; group two holds the formal accounting terms behind them.
note.cn: 第一组是最常被替换使用的足迹与碳声明术语；第二组是它们背后的正式核算术语。

entries.definition: The area of land and water needed to supply a population's resources and absorb its waste; it is measured in hectares, not tonnes.
entries.definitionCN: 供给人口资源并消纳其废物所需的土地与水域面积；以公顷计，而非吨。

entries.definition: The volume of fresh water used directly and indirectly by a product or activity, measured in litres or cubic metres.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或活动直接与间接耗用的淡水量，以升或立方米计。

entries.definition: A credit bought to compensate for emissions; it is supposed to cancel part of a footprint but is not itself one.
entries.definitionCN: 为补偿排放而购买的信用；它意在抵消部分足迹，但本身不是足迹。

entries.definition: The total emissions still permitted within a temperature limit; it looks forward, while a footprint records what has happened.
entries.definitionCN: 在某个温度上限内仍允许的排放总量；它向前看，而足迹记录已发生的事。

entries.definition: A formal, methodical count of emissions by source and sector; a footprint is often a simplified version of one.
entries.definitionCN: 按来源与部门系统统计排放的正式账目；足迹常是其简化版。

entries.definition: Emissions divided by output or revenue; it compares efficiency rather than total size.
entries.definitionCN: 排放除以产量或收入；比较的是效率，而非总量。

entries.definition: The systematic study of a product's impacts from cradle to grave; a product footprint is one of its outputs.
entries.definitionCN: 系统研究产品从摇篮到坟墓的影响；产品足迹是它的产出之一。

entries.definition: A state in which emissions are balanced by removals or offsets; it is a status claimed after a footprint is calculated.
entries.definitionCN: 排放由移除或抵消平衡的状态；它是算出足迹之后才声明的状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English and Latin roots and the real accounting logic.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的古英语与拉丁词根，以及真实的核算逻辑。

normal.en: footprint is a mark left behind: the phrase asks what mark your consumption leaves in the air.
normal.cn: footprint 是留下的印子：这个短语问的是你的消费在空气里留下什么印。

normal.en: print comes from premere, to press: a footprint is something pressed into a surface.
normal.cn: print 来自 premere「压」：足迹是被压进表面的东西。

normal.en: The unit is carbon dioxide equivalent, so methane and nitrous oxide are converted into one scale.
normal.cn: 单位是二氧化碳当量，于是甲烷与氧化亚氮被折算到同一把尺上。

normal.en: Three scopes: direct fuel, purchased power, and everything in the supply chain.
normal.cn: 三个范围：直接燃料、购入电力，以及供应链中的一切。

normal.en: The older cousin is ecological footprint, measured in land rather than gas.
normal.cn: 更早的表亲是生态足迹，用土地而非气体来计量。

abstract.en: A carbon footprint is a shadow cast in a gas nobody can see.
abstract.cn: 碳足迹是投在一种谁也看不见的气体里的影子。

abstract.en: It is a receipt for things already burned elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 它是一张为别处已经烧掉的东西开的收据。

abstract.en: Every number is a small confession.
abstract.cn: 每个数字都是一次小小的坦白。

examples.en: The label states the carbon footprint per portion.
examples.cn: 标签标明了每份的碳足迹。

examples.en: Firms audit their supply chains before publishing a carbon footprint.
examples.cn: 企业在公布碳足迹前会审计供应链。

examples.en: A carbon footprint measures emissions, not the damage they cause.
examples.cn: 碳足迹衡量的是排放，而不是排放造成的损害。

dict_mnemonic.text: carbon（碳）+ footprint（脚印）＝你的消费在空气里留下的排放印记；记三个范围：直接燃料、购入电力、供应链。

root: carbon（拉丁 carbo「木炭」）+ footprint（古英语 fōt「脚」+ print，源自拉丁 premere「压」）；短语为一九九〇年代生态足迹的碳版本延伸。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the number from its definition to its critiques: attributed total, event, product, household, standard, label, offset, national inventory and the objection that it individualises blame.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟这个数字从定义走到批评：归属总量、活动、产品、家庭、计量口径、标签、抵消、国家清单，以及它把责任个人化的反对意见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footprints walk from an oil well through a ship and a factory to a dinner plate, and each step leaves invisible gas that adds into one figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚印从油井经货轮与工厂走到餐盘，每一步都留下看不见的气体，最后加成一个数字。

branches.en: WHOLE AND PERSON: the attributed total, then the household version people can act on.
branches.cn: 整体与人：先是归属总量，再是普通人能行动的家庭版本。

branches.en: EVENTS AND GOODS: a gathering's travel and energy, then a product's whole life.
branches.cn: 活动与商品：先是集会的交通与能源，再是产品的整个生命。

branches.en: THE COMMON UNIT: every gas converted into carbon dioxide equivalent.
branches.cn: 共同单位：每种气体都折算成二氧化碳当量。

branches.en: COMMUNICATION AND CLAIM: the printed label, then the purchased offset.
branches.cn: 传播与声明：先是印出的标签，再是购买的抵消。

branches.en: SCALE AND CRITIQUE: national inventories, then the charge that the number shifts blame.
branches.cn: 尺度与批评：先是国家清单，再是指它转移责任的指控。

intro.en: Carbon footprint is a two-word phrase: a Latin-derived element name plus an English compound of foot and print.
intro.cn: carbon footprint 是两词短语：拉丁语源的元素名，加上由 foot 与 print 构成的英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin carbo gives carbon; Latin premere gives print through Old French; foot is native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 carbo 给出 carbon；拉丁 premere 经古法语给出 print；foot 则是本土古英语。

items.example: Carbo gave carbon.
items.exampleCN: carbo 给出 carbon。

items.meaning: the element counted in the phrase
items.example: Carbon is the common currency of the figure.
items.exampleCN: 碳是这个数字的共同货币。

items.example: Fōt survives unchanged in foot.
items.exampleCN: fōt 在 foot 中原样留存。

items.example: Premere produced Old French preinte.
items.exampleCN: premere 产生古法语 preinte。

items.meaning: a mark pressed into a surface
items.example: Preinte became English print.
items.exampleCN: preinte 变成英语 print。

items.meaning: a mark; to make a mark
items.example: Print supplies the second half of footprint.
items.exampleCN: print 提供 footprint 的后半截。

items.meaning: the mark a foot leaves; an occupied area
items.meaningCN: 脚留下的印记；占用的面积
items.example: Footprint widened from a track to an impact.
items.exampleCN: footprint 由脚印扩展为影响范围。

items.example: Emissions are what the footprint totals.
items.exampleCN: 排放正是足迹所汇总的东西。

items.example: An offset is not the same as a reduction.
items.exampleCN: 抵消并不等同于减排。

definition_zh: 催化剂；触媒；促进因素；引发变革的人或事
definition_en: a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed, or a person or event that causes change
core_image: 一块垫脚石：它自己不走路，却让别人跨过原本过不去的高墙
scene: 老师往双氧水里撒了一小撮二氧化锰，液体立刻翻腾起来。她说： The powder is a catalyst; it is still there when the reaction ends.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 catalyst 是「催化剂」（第 1、5 个义项：化学催化与不被消耗的物质）；句意：这粉末是催化剂，反应结束时它还在。图中可辨识物件：试管、气泡、黑色粉末、护目镜。

pos.zh: 催化剂；触媒；促进因素

derivatives.zh: 催化作用
催化的
催化；促成
