senses.title: A substance that speeds a reaction
senses.definition: a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being used up by it
senses.definitionCN: 能加快化学反应速率、而自身不被消耗的物质
senses.example: Platinum is an effective catalyst for this reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 铂是这一反应的有效催化剂。
senses.why: Greek katalyein meant 'to dissolve down', to loosen what holds something together. A catalyst loosens the barrier between reactants, so the reaction runs without it being consumed.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 katalyein 意为“向下溶解”，把束缚某物的东西松开。催化剂松开反应物之间的障碍，因此反应得以进行，而它自己不被消耗。

senses.title: A biological catalyst: an enzyme
senses.definition: a protein or other molecule in a living cell that speeds up a biochemical reaction
senses.definitionCN: 活细胞中加快生化反应的蛋白质或其他分子
senses.example: The enzyme acts as a catalyst for the breakdown of starch.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酶作为催化剂促进淀粉分解。
senses.why: Living cells perform the same trick at body temperature. The word transfers from the laboratory bench to the cell, but the function is identical.
senses.whyCN: 活细胞在体温下做着同样的把戏。这个词从实验台转移到细胞里，但功能完全相同。

senses.title: A person who makes things happen
senses.definition: a person who causes or speeds up a change without being the main actor
senses.definitionCN: 促成或加速变化、而自身并非主角的人
senses.example: She was the catalyst who brought the two sides together.
senses.exampleCN: 她正是把双方拉到一起的促成者。
senses.why: The chemical image transfers cleanly to people: someone lowers the barrier between parties, then steps aside. The person is not the reaction, only its enabler.
senses.whyCN: 化学意象干净地转移到人身上：某人降低双方之间的障碍，然后退到一旁。这个人不是反应本身，只是它的促成者。

senses.title: An event that sets off change
senses.definition: an event or development that triggers a larger process of change
senses.definitionCN: 触发更大变化过程的事件或发展
senses.example: The report became a catalyst for new legislation.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告成了新立法的催化剂。
senses.why: The event plays the role of the substance: it starts something larger without being the substance of that larger thing. History is imagined as a reaction waiting for a spark.
senses.whyCN: 事件扮演物质的角色：它启动了更大的事情，而自身并不构成那件事的实体。历史被想象成一个等待火花的反应。

senses.title: Something that is not consumed
senses.titleCN: 自身不被消耗的催化剂
senses.definition: a substance whose mass and composition remain essentially unchanged after the reaction
senses.definitionCN: 反应之后质量与成分基本不变的物质
senses.example: The catalyst can be filtered out and used again.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂可以滤出并再次使用。
senses.why: This is the defining property: the looser is not loosened. The word's usefulness in chemistry depends on this distinction from a reactant, which is consumed.
senses.whyCN: 这是定义性的特征：松开别的物质者本身不被松开。这个化学术语的有用之处，正在于它区别于会被消耗的反应物。

senses.title: The core of a catalytic converter
senses.definition: the active material inside a device that cleans exhaust gases, often platinum or another metal
senses.definitionCN: 净化废气装置中的活性材料，常为铂等金属
senses.example: The mechanic replaced the catalyst in the exhaust system.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工更换了排气系统中的催化芯。
senses.why: The device is named for its function, and the catalyst is its functional centre. Everyday car repair made the laboratory term into a replaceable part.
senses.whyCN: 这个装置以功能命名，而催化剂是它的功能核心。日常修车把一个实验室术语变成了可更换的零件。

senses.title: A policy catalyst
senses.definition: in policy and economics, a measure designed to encourage investment or activity that would not otherwise occur
senses.definitionCN: 政策与经济中，为鼓励原本不会发生的投资或活动而设计的措施
senses.example: The tax credit was intended as a catalyst for private investment.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税收抵免意在成为私人投资的催化剂。
senses.why: Government money is meant to lower the barrier, not to do the investing itself. The term gives policy a chemical shape: small input, large reaction.
senses.whyCN: 政府的钱意在降低障碍，而不是亲自投资。这个术语给政策一个化学形状：小投入，大反应。

senses.title: A character who drives the plot
senses.definition: in literature and drama, a character whose action sets the main conflict in motion
senses.definitionCN: 文学与戏剧中，其行动启动主要冲突的角色
senses.example: The messenger is the catalyst of the tragedy.
senses.exampleCN: 那个报信人是这场悲剧的催化剂。
senses.why: A play needs someone to lower the barrier between ordinary life and conflict. Critics borrowed the chemical word because it describes function, not importance.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧需要有人降低日常与冲突之间的障碍。评论家借用这个化学词，因为它描述的是功能，而不是重要性。

senses.title: A spark for a chain of events
senses.definition: a small trigger that sets off a sequence of much larger consequences
senses.definitionCN: 引发一连串更大后果的小触发点
senses.example: A single rumour proved to be the catalyst of the riot.
senses.exampleCN: 一则谣言成了那场骚乱的导火索。
senses.why: This is the loosest but most vivid extension: the catalyst is small, the chain is large. The word now measures disproportion between cause and effect.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽松也最生动的延伸：催化剂很小，链式后果很大。这个词如今度量的是因与果之间的不对称。

intro.en: Catalyst is a modern scientific coinage built from Greek parts. Its second element is not Latin and not English; it is Greek lyein, 'to loosen', the same root seen in analysis and electrolysis.
intro.cn: catalyst 是一个现代科学造词，由希腊语部件构成。它的第二成分不是拉丁语，也不是英语，而是希腊语 lyein“松开”，与 analysis、electrolysis 共享同一词根。

items.en: Kata- meant 'down, downwards, against'. It is the prefix in catalogue, catastrophe and category, and it gives the first element of katalysis.
items.cn: kata- 意为“向下、向下、对着”。它是 catalogue、catastrophe、category 中的前缀，也构成 katalysis 的第一部分。

items.en: Lyein meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve'. Its noun lysis, 'a loosening', is the second element of catalyst and the whole of the suffix -lysis in analysis and paralysis.
items.cn: lyein 意为“松开、解开、溶解”。其名词 lysis“松开”是 catalyst 的第二部分，也是 analysis、paralysis 中整个后缀 -lysis 的来源。

items.en: Katalysis meant 'a dissolving, a dissolution'. It described something being loosened down, not yet a chemical accelerator.
items.cn: katalysis 意为“溶解、消解”。它描述某物被向下松开，还不是化学上的加速剂。

items.en: The Swedish chemist Berzelius coined French and German terms for the phenomenon from Greek katalysis. The idea was that a substance loosens the bonds of others without being loosened itself.
items.cn: 瑞典化学家贝采利乌斯在 1835 年据希腊语 katalysis 造出法语与德语术语来命名这一现象。其想法是：某物质松开别的物质的键，而自身不被松开。

items.en: Catalyst was formed on the model of analysis and analyst, adding -ist for the agent. The exact date of the English coinage is approximate; it enters general use around 1900.
items.cn: catalyst 仿照 analysis 与 analyst 的模型，用 -ist 表示施动者。英语造词的确切年代为大致估计，约在 1900 年前后进入通用。

items.en: The chemical term spread into economics, politics and literary criticism in the 20th century. The metaphor is always the same: a small, unchanged enabler of a large change.
items.cn: 这个化学术语在 20 世纪扩散到经济、政治与文学批评。比喻始终如一：一个自身不变的小小促成者，带来巨大的变化。

note.en: The first group separates catalyst from its own derivatives and from a Greek-look-alike that comes from a different root. The second group compares things that cause change.
note.cn: 第一组把 catalyst 与自身派生词、以及来自另一词根的希腊式形近词分开。第二组比较引发变化的事物。

entries.definition: the process of accelerating a reaction, named before the agent. It is the process, while catalyst is the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 加快反应的过程，先于施动者被命名。它是过程，而 catalyst 是物质。

entries.definition: relating to catalysis. It describes the process or a device, not the substance itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与催化有关的。它描述过程或装置，而不是物质本身。

entries.definition: a device for throwing stones. Its second element is peltē 'shield' or pallein 'to hurl', not lyein.
entries.definitionCN: 投石装置。其第二成分是 peltē“盾”或 pallein“投掷”，不是 lyein。

entries.definition: a protein that catalyses a biochemical reaction. It is a kind of catalyst, but only in living systems.
entries.definitionCN: 催化生化反应的蛋白质。它是催化剂的一种，但只存在于生命系统中。

entries.definition: an event that sets something off at once. It stresses the sudden start, while catalyst stresses the enabling role.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻引发某事的事件。它强调突然启动，而 catalyst 强调促成作用。

entries.definition: a small thing that starts a large process. It is more literary and more sudden than catalyst.
entries.definitionCN: 启动大过程的小事物。它比 catalyst 更文学化、更突然。

entries.definition: a substance used in a reaction, which is consumed. It is the opposite role to a catalyst, which is not consumed.
entries.definitionCN: 参与反应并被消耗的物质。它与催化剂角色相反，后者不被消耗。

normalIntro.en: These hooks separate the Greek parts kata and lysis, and keep the two roles, substance and enabler, distinct.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把希腊部件 kata 与 lysis 分开，也把“物质”与“促成者”两种角色分清。

normal.en: Split it as kata + lyst: a downward loosener, not a cat and not a list.
normal.cn: 拆成 kata 加 lyst：向下的松开者，既不是猫，也不是清单。

normal.en: Link it to analysis: the -lysis part means loosening, so a catalyst loosens a barrier.
normal.cn: 把它连到 analysis：-lysis 表示松开，所以 catalyst 松开障碍。

normal.en: Remember the defining test: it comes out unchanged, ready to be used again.
normal.cn: 记住定义性检验：它出来时不变，可以再次使用。

normal.en: For people, picture someone holding a door open and then stepping aside.
normal.cn: 用在人身上，想象某人把门撑开，然后退到一旁。

normal.en: Keep catalyst and reactant apart: one is reused, the other is used up.
normal.cn: 把 catalyst 与 reactant 分开：一个被重复使用，一个被用尽。

abstract.en: Hold one function: lower the barrier, do not become the reaction.
abstract.cn: 抓住一个功能：降低障碍，不成为反应本身。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by field: chemistry, biology, people, events, devices, policy, drama, chains of consequence.
abstract.cn: 按领域分组义项：化学、生物、人、事件、装置、政策、戏剧、连锁后果。

abstract.en: Remember the direction of the metaphor: from a substance to a role, never to a mere cause.
abstract.cn: 记住比喻方向：从一种物质到一种角色，而不只是“原因”。

examples.en: The catalyst lowers the activation energy of the reaction.
examples.cn: 催化剂降低了反应的活化能。

examples.en: Her speech was the catalyst for a nationwide debate.
examples.cn: 她的演讲引发了全国性的讨论。

examples.en: Enzymes are catalysts that work at body temperature.
examples.cn: 酶是在体温下工作的催化剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“开特利斯特”：想象“开”一扇“特”别重的门，靠一块“利”器“斯特”别省力——它就是 catalyst 催化剂。

root: 希腊语 katalysis“溶解、消解”，由 kata-“向下、对着”加 lyein“松开、溶解”构成；1835 年贝采利乌斯据以造出催化术语，英语 catalyst 仿 analysis／analyst 加 -ist。与 analysis、electrolysis、paralysis 共享 -lysis。

sensesIntro.en: A catalyst is defined by a role, not by a substance: it lowers a barrier without becoming the thing that crosses it. Chemistry gave the word its precision, and every later use, from enzymes to reformers to plot devices, keeps that role intact. The nine senses differ mainly in what is being enabled.
sensesIntro.cn: catalyst 由角色而非物质定义：它降低障碍，而不成为跨越障碍的那件事。化学给了这个词精确性，后来从酶到改革者再到情节装置，每次使用都保留这个角色。九个义项的主要差别在于“被促成的是什么”。

core.en: Lower the barrier but stay outside the reaction: the unchanged enabler.
core.cn: 降低障碍而置身反应之外：自身不变的促成者。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: the substance that speeds a reaction and survives it.
branches.cn: 化学：加快反应并在反应后存留的物质。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: the enzyme doing the same work inside a cell.
branches.cn: 生物：在细胞内做同样工作的酶。

branches.en: AGENTS: a person, a policy or a character who enables others to act.
branches.cn: 施动者：促成他人行动的人、政策或角色。

branches.en: IGNITION: an event or rumour that starts a much larger chain.
branches.cn: 点火：启动更大链条的事件或谣言。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: the active core of a catalytic converter.
branches.cn: 装置：催化转化器中的活性核心。

intro.en: Catalyst is not built with Latin affixes but with Greek combining elements. The list shows -lysis across its relatives, and the modern suffixes -ic, -ize and -ly that grew on the English word.
intro.cn: catalyst 不是用拉丁词缀构成的，而是用希腊语组合成分。清单展示 -lysis 在各亲属词中的形态，以及英语词上长出的现代后缀 -ic、-ize、-ly。

latinIntro.en: There is no native Latin ancestor. The entries below are Latinized Greek borrowings: the learned Latin forms of lysis, analysis and catalysis, which carried the Greek root into European scientific vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 没有本族拉丁语祖先。下列条目是拉丁化的希腊借词：lysis、analysis、catalysis 的学术拉丁形式，它们把希腊词根带进了欧洲科学词汇。

items.meaning: a substance or agent that speeds up change
items.meaningCN: 加快变化的物质或施动者
items.example: The catalyst remained unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 催化剂保持不变。

items.meaning: the process of accelerating a reaction
items.example: Catalysis is central to industrial chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 催化是工业化学的核心。

items.example: The car has a catalytic converter.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车装有催化转化器。

items.meaning: to act as a catalyst for
items.example: The enzyme catalyzes the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 这种酶催化该反应。

items.example: The gas is cleaned catalytically.
items.exampleCN: 这种气体经催化净化。

items.meaning: a loosening apart; a detailed examination
items.example: The analysis broke the problem into parts.
items.exampleCN: 分析把问题拆成了几个部分。

items.example: Electrolysis splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.
items.exampleCN: 电解把水分解成氢和氧。

items.example: Hydrolysis breaks the polymer into monomers.
items.exampleCN: 水解把聚合物分解为单体。

items.meaning: a catalyst produced by a living system
items.example: The biocatalyst works at low temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这种生物催化剂在低温下工作。

items.meaning: the layer of catalyst material in a reactor
items.example: Gas passes through the catalyst bed.
items.exampleCN: 气体通过催化剂床层。

latinEntries.meaning: a loosening up; resolution into parts

definition_zh: 挂毯；织锦画；丰富交织的整体
definition_en: a heavy woven cloth with a picture or pattern, hung on a wall
core_image: 一幅巨大的编织画从墙上垂下，经纬线里藏着战争、狩猎与四季
scene: 修道院墙上垂下一幅巨幅挂毯，用经纬线讲出家族的往事。 A huge tapestry covered the abbey wall, telling the family's history in thread.
sceneCN: 这里指「织有图案的大型悬挂织物」（第 1 个义项：作为壁挂的织锦画）；句意为修道院墙上垂下一幅巨幅挂毯，用经纬线讲述家族往事。可辨识物件：墙面、垂下的织毯、狩猎图案、织线。

pos.zh: 挂毯；织锦画
（比喻）丰富交织的整体；错综复杂的组合

derivatives.zh: 用挂毯装饰的；织有图案的（由基础词加表示「覆有……」的后缀构成，语义偏移为状态）
挂毯织造者（由基础词与表示「制作者」的词复合，语义收窄为职业）
类似挂毯的；织纹丰富的（由基础词加表示「像……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）

senses.title: Woven pictorial hanging
senses.titleCN: 织有图案的大型悬挂织物
senses.definition: a heavy hand-woven cloth with a pictorial design, usually hung on a wall
senses.definitionCN: 手工织成、带图案的厚重织物，通常挂在墙上
senses.example: A huge tapestry covered the abbey wall.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院墙上垂下一幅巨幅挂毯。
senses.why: The word first names the object. It is woven rather than painted, so the picture is built into the cloth thread by thread.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指物件。它是织出来的，而不是画上去的，所以画面是一根线一根线织进布里的。

senses.title: The weaving craft
senses.definition: the craft or industry of weaving pictorial hangings on a loom
senses.definitionCN: 在织机上织造图画挂毯的手艺或行业
senses.example: The town lived by tapestry for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇靠挂毯织造业生活了三百年。
senses.why: A tapestry takes months at a loom, so the making became a named trade with its own workshops and masters.
senses.whyCN: 一幅挂毯要在织机上耗费数月，制作因此成为有作坊、有师傅的专门行业。

senses.title: A decorative wall hanging
senses.definition: a large decorative cloth hung on a wall to furnish or warm a room
senses.definitionCN: 挂在墙上用于布置或保暖的大幅装饰织物
senses.example: The hall was warmed by heavy tapestries.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅靠厚重的挂毯保暖。
senses.why: Before wallpaper, a woven hanging covered a cold stone wall. The object was furniture as much as picture.
senses.whyCN: 在壁纸出现之前，编织悬挂物用来覆盖冰冷的石墙。它既是画，也是家具。

senses.title: Needlework on canvas
senses.definition: a piece of needlework worked on canvas in coloured wools, also called tapestry work
senses.definitionCN: 用彩色毛线在帆布上绣成的作品，也称绒线绣
senses.example: She finished the tapestry with a fine needle.
senses.exampleCN: 她用细针完成了这幅绒线绣。
senses.why: Handwork that covers a whole canvas with stitches came to share the name, because it too builds a picture from many separate threads.
senses.whyCN: 把整块帆布用针脚盖满的手工也共享了这个名称，因为它同样用许多分离的线构成画面。

senses.title: A woven historical record
senses.titleCN: 以织物形式留存的历史叙述
senses.definition: a hanging that records events, genealogies or legends as a visual chronicle
senses.definitionCN: 以图像编年方式记录事件、世系或传说的悬挂织物
senses.example: The tapestry records the duke's voyage in seventy scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅挂毯用七十个场景记录了公爵的航行。
senses.why: A hanging can be read across a room. When few people could read text, a woven sequence of scenes served as a public record.
senses.whyCN: 挂在墙上的织物可以横跨整间屋子被阅读。在识字者不多的年代，连续的编织场景就是公共记录。

senses.title: A complex interwoven whole
senses.definition: a whole made of many interwoven parts, such as peoples, stories or events
senses.definitionCN: 由许多相互交织的部分构成的整体，如族群、故事或事件
senses.example: The district is a tapestry of old trades and new arrivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这个街区是旧行业与新来者的交织体。
senses.why: The visual structure becomes a metaphor: separate threads cross without replacing one another, and the pattern exists only because they do.
senses.whyCN: 视觉结构成为隐喻：不同的线交错而过，彼此不替换对方，图案正因为它们交错才存在。

senses.title: Rich variety of life
senses.titleCN: 人生或历史的丰富多样
senses.definition: the varied, colourful complexity of a life, a culture or a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段人生、一种文化或一个时期的多样而丰富的复杂性
senses.example: The memoir covers a rich tapestry of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这本回忆录写尽了乡村生活的丰富交织。
senses.why: The phrase 'a rich tapestry' generalizes the hanging into any dense mixture that rewards close reading.
senses.whyCN: 「丰富的织锦」这一说法把挂毯一般化，指任何值得细看的密集混合。

senses.title: An interwoven abstract pattern
senses.definition: a pattern or structure in which many strands cross and hold together
senses.definitionCN: 许多线索交错并彼此维系而成的图案或结构
senses.example: The novel's plot is a tapestry of parallel lives.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的情节是平行人生的交织图案。
senses.why: The most abstract sense keeps only the geometry: crossing strands that make a surface without any picture at all.
senses.whyCN: 最抽象的义项只保留几何关系：交错的线构成一个表面，却完全不需要画面。

intro.en: Tapestry came through Old French from a word for carpet. The same Greek noun that gave Latin its word for a rug also gave French its word for a hanging. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tapestry 经古法语来自一个表示「地毯」的词。给拉丁语提供「毯子」说法的同一个希腊名词，也为法语提供了「悬挂织物」的说法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek tapēs (genitive tapētos) meant 'carpet, heavy cloth'. Its origin is source uncertain and it is generally believed to be a loanword from an Anatolian language rather than an inherited Greek word.
items.cn: 希腊 tapēs（属格 tapētos）意为「地毯、厚重织物」。其来源属「来源不确定」，一般认为它是来自安纳托利亚某语言的借词，而非希腊语固有词。

items.en: Latin tapete and tapetum, both 'carpet or coverlet', were borrowings of the Greek noun; Latin did not inherit the word.
items.cn: 拉丁 tapete 与 tapetum 都意为「地毯、床罩」，是那个希腊名词的借词；拉丁语并未继承这个词。

items.en: Old French tapis 'carpet' came from the Latin form. Its derived tapisserie first meant a workshop of hangings and then the hangings themselves.
items.cn: 古法语 tapis「地毯」来自拉丁形式。由它派生的 tapisserie 先指制作悬挂物的作坊，再指悬挂物本身。

items.en: English borrowed tapestry in the fifteenth century for a pictorial wall hanging, at a time when such hangings were among the most valuable objects a household owned.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 tapestry，指带图案的壁挂；当时这类悬挂物是家庭最贵重的财产之一。

items.en: By the nineteenth century writers used the word for any rich interweaving of events or cultures, and the metaphor remains the most common use outside museums.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，作家用它指事件或文化的丰富交织；在博物馆之外，这一比喻义如今是最常见的用法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Greek origin of tapēs is unresolved, and any older form proposed for it is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：tapēs 在希腊语之前的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的更早形式都属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same word that name related things; group two holds other words for large decorative hangings.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一个词构成、指相关事物的形式；第二组是其他表示大型装饰悬挂物的词。

entries.definition: covered with or shown in tapestry; it describes a surface, while tapestry names the object.
entries.definitionCN: 覆有挂毯的；以挂毯表现的。它描述表面，而 tapestry 指物件。

entries.definition: a large blunt needle used in wool needlework; the compound names a tool, not a hanging.
entries.definitionCN: 绒线绣用的大号钝针；这个复合词指工具，而非悬挂织物。

entries.definition: a weaving structure in which the coloured threads form the pattern itself; it names a technique, not a finished hanging.
entries.definitionCN: 彩色线本身构成图案的织造结构；它指技法，而非成品挂毯。

entries.definition: a crochet technique that carries one colour while working another; the compound names a method rather than a wall hanging.
entries.definitionCN: 一种一边带线一边换色的钩织技法；这个复合词指方法，而非壁挂。

entries.definition: a tapestry, especially one from the town of Arras; the word comes from the place name, not from the tapestry root.
entries.definitionCN: 挂毯，尤指阿拉斯城出产的；这个词来自地名，而非挂毯词根。

entries.definition: any decorative cloth hung on a wall; it says nothing about weaving or a pictorial design.
entries.definitionCN: 挂在墙上的任何装饰织物；不涉及织造或图案。

entries.definition: decoration stitched onto existing cloth; a tapestry is woven as a whole, while embroidery is added to a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 缝在既有布料上的装饰；挂毯整体织成，刺绣则加在表面上。

entries.definition: a floor covering; the French ancestor of tapestry meant carpet, and the two words separated when hangings moved from floor to wall.
entries.definitionCN: 地面覆盖物；挂毯的法语祖词本指地毯，当悬挂物从地面移到墙上，两词才分开。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The French ancestor meant carpet, which explains why a hanging and a floor covering once shared a name.
normal.cn: 法语祖词本指地毯，这解释了为什么壁挂与地面覆盖物曾共用一个名称。

normal.en: The Greek noun behind it is generally believed to be a borrowed word, not an inherited one.
normal.cn: 它背后的希腊名词一般认为是个借词，而非继承词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show both object and metaphor: a wall tapestry, a rich tapestry of cultures.
normal.cn: 固定搭配同时展示实物与比喻：壁挂织毯、丰富的文化交织。

normal.en: A tapestry is woven, not painted, so the picture lives in the threads.
normal.cn: 挂毯是织出来的，不是画出来的，所以画面活在经纬线里。

normal.en: The historical hanging was read like a chronicle across a room.
normal.cn: 历史上的挂毯可以横跨整间屋子当作编年史来读。

abstract.en: Picture many coloured threads crossing without ever replacing one another.
abstract.cn: 想象许多彩色线交错而过，却从不替换对方。

abstract.en: Picture a family story that can only be told by weaving several lives together.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只能把几段人生织在一起才讲得完的家族故事。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that speaks only when you step back far enough to see the whole pattern.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，只有退得足够远、看见整幅图案时才会说话。

examples.en: The tapestry took four weavers almost a year to finish.
examples.cn: 这幅挂毯用了四名织工将近一年才完成。

examples.en: Visitors read the battle across the tapestry from left to right.
examples.cn: 参观者从左到右读着挂毯上的战役。

examples.en: The memoir is a tapestry of farm work, gossip and grief.
examples.cn: 这本回忆录是农活、闲话与悲伤的交织。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「毯铺斯特里」—— 毯子铺在墙上，织出一整幅画 → 挂毯

root: 经古法语 tapisserie、tapis「地毯」上溯至拉丁 tapete、tapetum，再上溯至希腊 tapēs「地毯、厚织物」；希腊词一般认为借自安纳托利亚语言，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one woven surface: a pictorial hanging, the craft that makes it, the wall object, the needlework cousin, the historical chronicle, and then three metaphors built on crossing threads.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一块编织表面展开：带图案的挂毯、制作它的工艺、墙上的物件、绒线绣近亲、历史编年，最后是三个由交错经纬线构成的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long woven panel on a wall, its threads crossing to hold a story.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的一长幅编织物，经纬线交错，托住一个故事。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the word begins with heavy cloth carrying a woven picture.
branches.cn: 物件：这个词从织有图案的厚重布料开始。

branches.en: MAKING IT: loom weaving and canvas needlework are two ways of building a picture from threads.
branches.cn: 制作：织机织造与帆布刺绣，都是用线构成画面的两种方式。

branches.en: IN THE ROOM: hung on a wall, the cloth becomes furniture and warmth.
branches.cn: 在房间里：挂到墙上，这块布就成了家具与温暖。

branches.en: AS RECORD: a sequence of scenes turns the hanging into a public chronicle.
branches.cn: 作为记录：连续的场景把这幅悬挂物变成公共编年史。

branches.en: THREE METAPHORS: a mixed society, a rich life and an abstract pattern all keep the image of crossing threads.
branches.cn: 三个比喻：混合社会、丰富人生与抽象图案，都保留交错经纬线的意象。

intro.en: Tapestry is a French noun formed with a suffix of trade and place, built on a word for carpet that entered Europe from Greek.
intro.cn: tapestry 是一个法语名词，由表示行业与场所的后缀构成，其词干来自一个从希腊语进入欧洲的「地毯」词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tapete and tapetum are themselves borrowings of Greek tapēs, so the Latin forms record the word's passage rather than its invention.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tapete 与 tapetum 本身就是希腊 tapēs 的借词，因此这些拉丁形式记录的是这个词的传递，而不是它的创造。

items.example: Greek tapēs is generally believed to be a loanword.
items.exampleCN: 希腊 tapēs 一般认为是个借词。

items.example: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as tapete.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把希腊名词借作 tapete。

items.structure: Old French tapis, from Latin tapete
items.example: French tapis kept the carpet sense.
items.exampleCN: 法语 tapis 保留了地毯义。

items.structure: -erie (Old French suffix of place or trade)
items.meaning: a workshop or a collective product
items.example: Tapisserie first meant a hanging workshop.
items.exampleCN: tapisserie 最初指制作悬挂物的作坊。

items.example: The tapestry shows a hunting scene.
items.exampleCN: 这幅挂毯表现狩猎场景。

items.meaning: hung with or shown in tapestry
items.meaningCN: 用挂毯装饰的；织成图案的
items.example: The chamber was tapestried with hunting scenes.
items.exampleCN: 这间厅堂挂满狩猎图案的织毯。

items.example: The tapestry-maker dyed his own wool.
items.exampleCN: 织毯人自己染羊毛。

items.example: The field is tapestry-like from the air.
items.exampleCN: 从空中看，田野像一幅挂毯。

items.meaning: a large needle for wool needlework
items.example: Use a tapestry needle for the thick wool.
items.exampleCN: 织厚羊毛要用大号绒线针。

definition_zh: （学校）财务主管；（英国大学）司库；学费奖学金领取者
definition_en: the officer in charge of money at a school or college; also a student holding a bursary
core_image: 账房里管钱袋的先生，钥匙串在腰间叮当作响
scene: 学院账房里，管钱的先生正核对一叠账单。 The bursar approved the budget for the new library.
sceneCN: 这里 bursar 是「财务主管、司库」（第 1 个义项：负责学校钱账的职员）；句意是这位司库批准了新图书馆的预算。

pos.zh: （学校、学院的）财务主管；司库
领取助学金（奖学金）的学生

derivatives.zh: 由 bursar 加 -y 构成，义为「助学金；奖学金」

由 re- 加同源词根构成，义为「偿还，报销」

senses.title: The money officer of a school or college
senses.definition: the official responsible for the finances and accounts of a school, college or similar institution
senses.definitionCN: 负责学校、学院等机构财务与账目的职员
senses.example: The bursar signed off every payment the college made.
senses.exampleCN: 学院的每笔付款都由司库签字核准。
senses.why: The word comes from the purse that held the money, and the officer keeps that purse.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自装钱的钱袋，主管就是守住钱袋的人。

senses.title: A student who holds a bursary
senses.definition: a student whose studies are paid for by a grant or scholarship, especially at a British school
senses.definitionCN: 由补助金或奖学金资助学业的学生，多见于英国学校
senses.example: He entered the school as a bursar with his fees fully paid.
senses.exampleCN: 他以奖学金生的身份入学，学费全免。
senses.why: The purse that pays the institution also pays the student, so the funded learner takes the purse's name.
senses.whyCN: 钱袋既供机构开销，也资助学生，受助者便以钱袋为名。

senses.title: A manager of a monastery's temporal affairs
senses.definition: in some religious houses, the monk appointed to manage property and money matters
senses.definitionCN: 在某些修会中受命管理财产与钱财事务的修士
senses.example: The old bursar kept the abbey's ledgers in careful order.
senses.exampleCN: 老管事把修道院的账簿整理得井井有条。
senses.why: Monasteries ran large estates, so they needed a purse-keeper of their own.
senses.whyCN: 修道院经营大量产业，同样需要一位管钱袋的人。

intro.en: Bursar goes back to a Late Latin word for a bag or purse, the holder of money.
intro.cn: bursar 源自后期拉丁语中指袋子、钱袋的词，即掌管钱财之人。

items.en: bursa meant a bag made of hide, later a purse of money.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 bursa 指皮革做的袋子，后指钱袋。

items.en: bursarius named the officer who kept the purse of an institution.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 bursarius 指为机构掌管钱袋的职员。

items.en: boussiere and bourser carried the purse sense into French.
items.cn: 古法语 boussiere、bourser 把钱袋义带入法语。

items.en: bursar entered English for the finance officer of a college, then for a funded student.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪 bursar 进入英语，先指学院财务官，后指受助学生。

items.en: The academic senses survive, while the related bursary names the grant itself.
items.cn: 如今学校义项保留，同族的 bursary 指助学金本身。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the purse root; the near-meaning group lists other money-handling roles.
note.cn: 形近组同出「钱袋」词根；近义组是其他管钱的角色。

entries.definitionCN: 支出，支付，同出钱袋词根

entries.definition: an officer who manages an estate for its owner

entries.definition: a college officer keeping official records
entries.definitionCN: 注册主任，管理学籍档案的职员

normalIntro.cn: 盯住钱袋：无论在账房还是在课堂，握钱袋者即 bursar。

normal.en: The root bursa means purse, the bag of money.
normal.cn: 词根 bursa 意为钱袋，装钱的袋子。

normal.en: Disburse means to let money out of the purse.
normal.cn: disburse 指把钱从钱袋里发放出去。

normal.en: Reimburse literally means to fill the purse again.
normal.cn: reimburse 字面义是「重新装满钱袋」，即偿还。

normal.en: Bursary is the purse given to a funded student.
normal.cn: bursary 是发给受助学生的那只钱袋。

normal.en: In anatomy bursa kept the bag meaning as a sac.
normal.cn: 解剖学里 bursa 保留「袋」义，指滑囊。

abstract.cn: 听腰间挂着钱袋的钥匙串叮当作响。

abstract.en: See the ledger open and the seal pressed on each page.
abstract.cn: 看账簿翻开，每页都盖了印。

abstract.en: Picture a scholar whose fees arrive in a small purse.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生，他的学费装在一只小钱袋里送来。

examples.en: The bursar explained the fee increase to the parents.
examples.cn: 财务主管向家长们解释了涨费的原因。

examples.en: She won a place at the school as a bursar.
examples.cn: 她以奖学金生的身份获得了这所学校的名额。

examples.en: Disbursements from the fund are authorised by the bursar.
examples.cn: 基金支出均由财务主管核准。

sensesIntro.cn: 从一只拉丁钱袋长出三个义项：学院管钱的司库、从钱袋受助的学生，以及旧时修道院的庶务管事。

core_image: 一只手在文件上盖下印章，把一个名字正式按在某块土地上

senses.title: A name or title
senses.titleCN: 名称：给它一个正式的叫法
senses.definition: the name or title by which something is officially known
senses.definitionCN: 某物被正式使用的名称或称号
senses.example: The plant's scientific designation is longer than its common name.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的科学名称比它的俗名长。
senses.why: designare means 'to mark out'. A designation is the mark left on a thing by naming it, so the name becomes the official handle.
senses.whyCN: designare 意为“标出”。designation 是命名在事物上留下的标记，于是这个名字成了官方把手。

senses.title: Official recognition of status
senses.titleCN: 官方认定：给它一个身份
senses.definition: the formal act of declaring that something has a particular status
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某物具有某种身份的行为
senses.example: The designation of the area as a nature reserve blocked new construction.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区被认定为自然保护区后，新建设被阻止。
senses.why: The mark here is legal rather than verbal. Officials designate a site by writing its status into the record, and the status changes what may be done there.
senses.whyCN: 这里的标记是法律性的，而非口头性的。官员把某地的身份写入记录，这个身份就改变了那里允许做什么。

senses.title: Appointment to a post
senses.definition: the act of appointing someone to a particular role or office
senses.definitionCN: 把某人任命到某个角色或职位的行为
senses.example: Her designation as chair took effect in January.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为主席，于一月生效。
senses.why: To designate a person for a post is to mark that person as occupying it. The noun names the appointment rather than the person's abilities.
senses.whyCN: 把某人指定到某职位，就是标记此人在其位。名词命名的是任命行为，而非此人的能力。

senses.title: A label or code
senses.definition: a short label, code or symbol used to identify something
senses.definitionCN: 用于识别某物的简短标签、代码或符号
senses.example: Each sample carries a designation such as B-14.
senses.exampleCN: 每个样本都带有一个如 B-14 的编号。
senses.why: A code is a mark reduced to its smallest form. The noun still names the identifying mark, even when the mark is only letters and digits.
senses.whyCN: 代码是被压缩到最小形式的标记。即使标记只是字母和数字，这个名词仍命名识别标记。

senses.title: Marking out an area
senses.titleCN: 划定：在地图上圈出这一块
senses.definition: the marking of land or space for a particular use or restriction
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途或限制而标出土地或空间
senses.example: Zoning designations decide which plots may hold factories.
senses.exampleCN: 分区划定决定哪些地块可以建工厂。
senses.why: This sense is almost literal: a boundary is drawn on a map, and the enclosed area is designated. The pen does the work that designare describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项几乎是字面的：地图上画一条界线，圈内的区域就被划定了。笔做的正是 designare 描述的工作。

senses.title: Target marking
senses.titleCN: 目标指定：把要打的东西标出来
senses.definition: in military or technical use, the selection and marking of a target for action
senses.definitionCN: 军事或技术用语中，选定并标出行动目标
senses.example: Laser designation guided the missile to the correct building.
senses.exampleCN: 激光目标指定把导弹引向正确的大楼。
senses.why: A target must be marked before it can be hit. The technical phrase keeps the physical gesture of pointing something out with a mark.
senses.whyCN: 目标必须先被标出才能被击中。这个技术短语保留了“用标记指出某物”的物理手势。

senses.title: A classifying label in taxonomy
senses.titleCN: 分类命名：给物种一个学名
senses.definition: the formal naming of a species or group in scientific classification
senses.definitionCN: 科学分类中为物种或类群正式命名
senses.example: The new beetle received its designation after the museum's founder.
senses.exampleCN: 这种新甲虫以博物馆创始人的名字命名。
senses.why: Scientific naming is marking with precision: the designation fixes a specimen to a category, so that every later record can point to the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 科学命名是精确标记： designation 把标本固定到某个类别，使后来所有记录都指向同一物。

senses.title: The act of pointing out in speech
senses.titleCN: 指称：用词点到那个对象
senses.definition: in philosophy and linguistics, the referring of a term to a particular object
senses.definitionCN: 哲学与语言学中，一个词项指向特定对象
senses.example: The article examines how proper names achieve designation.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章考察专有名词如何实现指称。
senses.why: Designation in this technical sense is pointing with a word. The mark is not on paper but in the relation between a term and its object.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义中的指称是用词来指。标记不在纸上，而在词项与对象之间的关系里。

intro.en: Designation comes from Latin designatio 'a marking out', from designare, de- 'out' plus signare 'to mark' and signum 'a sign'. The word has always meant putting a mark on something to identify it.
intro.cn: designation 来自拉丁 designatio“标出”，来自 designare，由 de-“出”加 signare“标记”和 signum“记号”构成。这个词一直表示在某物上留下识别标记。

items.en: signum meant 'a mark, sign, token'. It is the source of sign, signal and signature, so the family is about visible marks that carry meaning.
items.cn: signum 意为“标记、记号、信物”。它是 sign、signal、signature 的来源，因此这个词族关乎承载意义的可见标记。

items.en: signare 'to mark, seal, sign' turns the noun into a verb. A seal pressed into wax is the clearest image: a mark that makes a claim official.
items.cn: signare“标记、盖章、签名”把名词变成动词。压进蜡里的印章是最清楚的画面：一个使主张生效的标记。

items.en: designare adds de- 'out, completely' to signare, giving 'to mark out, point out, appoint'. Latin used it for choosing a successor as well as for drawing boundaries.
items.cn: designare 给 signare 加 de-“出、完全”，意为“标出、指出、指定”。拉丁语既用它表示选定继任者，也表示划界。

items.en: designatio named the act of marking out and the mark produced. English borrowed the stem designation- and formed the noun with -ion.
items.cn: designatio 命名标出的动作及产生的标记。英语借入 designation- 词干，用 -ion 构成名词。

items.en: English uses designation from the 15th century for a name, appointment or boundary. The exact first record is uncertain because designate entered separately.
items.cn: 英语从 15 世纪起用 designation 表示名称、任命或界线。由于 designate 是另行进入的，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: In the 20th century the word spread to zoning, taxonomy, military targeting and philosophy of language. Each field marks a different kind of object with a name.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到分区规划、分类学、军事目标指定和语言哲学。每个领域都用名称标记不同种类的对象。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sign- stem through different prefixes and endings; the near-meaning group separates naming, appointing, marking and classifying.
note.cn: 形近组经不同前缀与词尾共享 sign- 词干；近义组区分命名、任命、标记与分类。

entries.definition: to officially choose, name or mark; the verb names the act behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 正式选定、命名或标出；这个动词命名名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: serving to designate or point out; the -ive suffix turns the action into a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 用于指称或标示的；-ive 后缀把动作变成性质。

entries.definition: a plan or pattern; it shares signum but shifted from 'mark out' to 'plan out' in English.
entries.definitionCN: 设计；图案；方案。它共享 signum，但在英语中从“标出”转变为“规划出”。

entries.definition: the word by which a person or thing is known; a designation is more formal and often official.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物被称呼的词；designation 更正式，常带官方色彩。

entries.definition: a name showing rank or office; it is narrower than designation, which also covers codes and statuses.
entries.definitionCN: 显示等级或职位的名称；比 designation 窄，后者也包括代号与身份认定。

entries.definition: the act of choosing someone for a position; it matches sense 3 but does not cover naming or marking.
entries.definitionCN: 选定某人担任职位；对应第 3 义，但不涵盖命名或标记。

entries.definition: the act of arranging things into classes; designation names the label, classification names the system.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物分入类别的行为；designation 命名标签，classification 命名体系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'out' + signum 'mark': designation is a mark put out where everyone can read it.
normal.cn: de-“出”+ signum“记号”：designation 是摆出来给所有人读的标记。

normal.en: sign, signal, signature and designate all share signum; the family is about visible marks.
normal.cn: sign、signal、signature、designate 都共享 signum，这个词族关乎可见标记。

normal.en: The usual pattern is designation as: the mark names the new status.
normal.cn: 常用结构是 designation as：标记命名了新身份。

normal.en: In planning, remember land designation: the map mark decides what may be built.

definition_zh: 非线性的；非直线的；不成比例的；（叙事、剪辑）不按固定顺序的
definition_en: not forming a straight line and not changing in direct proportion, or not following one fixed sequence
core_image: 一条越走越陡的曲线，起点平缓，末端几乎竖起来
scene: 同一组数据被画成曲线，输入翻倍时输出涨了三倍。 The response became nonlinear once the amplifier reached its limit.
sceneCN: 这里 nonlinear 指「输出与输入不再成比例」（第 2 个义项：不成正比的响应）；句意：放大器到达极限后，响应就变成非线性的了。图中可辨识物件：曲线图、放大器、输入旋钮、输出表。

senses.title: Not a straight line on a graph
senses.definition: appearing as a curve rather than a straight line when plotted
senses.definitionCN: 画在图上呈曲线，而不是直线
senses.example: The fitted curve is nonlinear and bends sharply at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 拟合出的曲线是非线性的，末端急剧弯曲。
senses.why: Non- negates linear, and linear first meant line-shaped, so the word begins as a denial of straightness.
senses.whyCN: non- 否定 linear，而 linear 首先表示线形，所以这个词一开始就是对「直」的否认。

senses.title: Out of proportion to the input
senses.definition: responding by a different ratio, so that doubling the input more than doubles or less than doubles the output
senses.definitionCN: 响应的比率不同，输入加倍时输出可能超过两倍，也可能不到两倍
senses.example: The spring becomes nonlinear under heavy loads.
senses.exampleCN: 这根弹簧在重载下表现出非线性。
senses.why: Proportional change draws a straight line, so losing proportion and losing straightness are one event.
senses.whyCN: 按比例变化画出来是直线，因此失去比例与失去直线性其实是同一件事。

senses.title: Containing higher powers or products
senses.definition: containing squared, cubed or multiplied variables, so that no single straight-line solution exists
senses.definitionCN: 含平方、立方或变量乘积，因而没有单一直线解
senses.example: That nonlinear equation has two separate solutions.
senses.exampleCN: 那个非线性方程有两个不同的解。
senses.why: A squared term bends the curve, which is the algebraic reason the equation can no longer be a line.
senses.whyCN: 平方项让曲线弯折，这就是方程不再是直线的代数原因。

senses.title: Sensitive dynamics that do not settle
senses.titleCN: 对初值敏感、难以收敛的动态
senses.definition: describing systems whose behaviour is sensitive to small changes and cannot be predicted by simple proportional rules
senses.definitionCN: 描述对微小变化敏感、无法用简单比例规则预测的系统
senses.example: Weather is a classic nonlinear system with sensitive beginnings.
senses.exampleCN: 天气是典型的非线性系统，初始条件十分敏感。
senses.why: When outputs feed back into inputs, small differences grow, and the tidy line of proportionality disappears.
senses.whyCN: 当输出又回到输入形成反馈，微小差异会被放大，成比例的整齐直线就消失了。

senses.title: A story that jumps in time
senses.definition: telling events out of chronological order, with flashbacks, parallel threads or repeated scenes
senses.definitionCN: 不按时间顺序叙述，使用倒叙、并行线索或重复场景
senses.example: The novel uses a nonlinear structure that begins at the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说采用非线性结构，从葬礼写起。
senses.why: A sequence that does not advance in one straight line is pictured as a bent path, the same image as the graph.
senses.whyCN: 不沿一条直线推进的顺序被想象成弯折的路径，与图上的曲线是同一意象。

senses.title: Distorted output in electronics
senses.definition: producing an output that no longer matches the input waveform, so that the signal is clipped or bent
senses.definitionCN: 输出不再与输入波形一致，信号被削顶或弯折
senses.example: Push the microphone too hard and the recording turns nonlinear.
senses.exampleCN: 话筒推得太狠，录音就会变成非线性。
senses.why: Clipping destroys the one-to-one relation between input and output, which is exactly the loss of a straight line.
senses.whyCN: 削顶破坏了输入与输出的一一对应，正相当于失去那条直线。

senses.title: Editing with instant access
senses.definition: editing video or audio by jumping directly to any frame, rather than winding through tape in order
senses.definitionCN: 直接跳到任意画面进行剪辑，而不是沿磁带顺序卷动
senses.example: Nonlinear editing lets the editor cut the last scene first.
senses.exampleCN: 非线性剪辑让剪辑师可以先剪最后一场。
senses.why: Tape forces a single forward path; random access breaks that path, so the workflow is called nonlinear.
senses.whyCN: 磁带只允许一条向前的路径，随机访问打破这条路径，于是这种流程被称为非线性。

senses.title: Thinking in leaps rather than steps
senses.titleCN: 跳跃式而非逐步式思考
senses.definition: reasoning by sudden connections and side paths instead of a single orderly chain of steps
senses.definitionCN: 靠突然的联想与旁路推理，而不是一条整齐的步骤链
senses.example: Her nonlinear thinking found a link the linear plan had missed.
senses.exampleCN: 她的跳跃式思考找到了线性计划漏掉的关联。
senses.why: Thought that branches and loops is drawn as a curve or a network, not as the straight path of step-by-step logic.
senses.whyCN: 会分叉、会回环的思路被画成曲线或网络，而不是逐步逻辑的直路。

intro.en: Nonlinear is an English compound of non- 'not' and linear, which itself goes back to Latin linea 'line'. The word is not a Latin formation: Latin supplied the negative particle and the adjective separately. It spread with mathematics and engineering in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nonlinear 是英语复合词，由 non-「不」加 linear 构成，而 linear 可上溯到拉丁 linea「线」。这个词并非拉丁语造词：拉丁语分别提供了否定词与形容词。它随数学与工程在十九、二十世纪推广。年代均为约数。

items.en: Non was a Latin adverb and negative particle meaning 'not'; English uses it freely as a prefix, as in nonsense and nonstop.
items.cn: non 是拉丁副词与否定小品词，意为「不」；英语自由地把它当否定前缀用，如 nonsense 与 nonstop。

items.en: Linea 'line, thread' is the source of linear; the geometric meaning of straightness is the part that non- denies.
items.cn: linea「线、线绳」是 linear 的来源；non- 否定的正是其中「直」这一几何含义。

items.en: English joined non- and linear to name anything that departs from a straight line or a fixed ratio; the compound is English, not Latin.
items.cn: 英语把 non- 与 linear 拼在一起，指任何偏离直线或固定比例的事物；这个复合词属英语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: Nineteenth-century work on differential equations and mechanics gave nonlinear equations and nonlinear systems their technical footing.
items.cn: 十九世纪关于微分方程与力学的工作，为非线性方程与非线性系统奠定了技术基础。

items.en: Chaos theory, electronics and digital editing each took the word for a different departure from a predictable straight path.
items.cn: 混沌理论、电子学与数字剪辑各自用这个词表示一种对可预测直路的偏离。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the word is a transparent English compound of non- and linear, so its formation is not in doubt; only the earliest recorded English use is undated. The deeper origin of linea is not established, and no reconstructed root is asserted.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个词是 non- 与 linear 构成的透明英语复合词，构词方式并不存疑；只是英语最早用例没有确切年代。linea 的更早来源无定论，此处不给出重构词根。

note.en: Group one holds the linear stock, where non- reverses or names the absence of straightness; group two holds words for curves, growth and disorder that are often confused with nonlinear.
note.cn: 第一组是 linear 一族，non- 在其中表示否定或「缺乏直线性」；第二组是常与非线性混淆的曲线、增长与无序类词。

entries.definition: Straight and proportional; the exact property that nonlinear denies.

entries.definition: The quality of being nonlinear, often written with a hyphen in British texts.

entries.definition: Of direct descent; it looks related but belongs to family trees, not curves.

entries.definition: Bent rather than straight; it describes the picture but says nothing about proportionality.

entries.definition: Growing by a constant ratio; a frequent nonlinear pattern, but not every nonlinear relation is exponential.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定比率增长；一种常见的非线性形态，但并非所有非线性关系都是指数式。

entries.definition: Extremely sensitive to initial conditions; it names a kind of dynamics, not a departure from a line.
entries.definitionCN: 对初始条件极敏感；命名一种动态行为，而不是偏离直线。

entries.definition: Not even or uniform; an everyday word that carries no mathematical definition.
entries.definitionCN: 不均匀、不规整；日常用词，没有数学定义。

examples.cn: 非线性剪辑取代了旧的磁带流程。

examples.en: A nonlinear narrative can feel confusing if the jumps are not motivated.
examples.cn: 如果跳跃缺少动机，非线性叙事会让人困惑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「non（不）+ linear（线）」——不是直线：非线性的、不成比例的

root: 英语复合词：non-（拉丁副词「不」）+ linear（拉丁 linearis，出自 linea「线」）。复合本身是英语构词，不是拉丁词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all deny one straight path: a bent curve, a broken proportion, higher powers, sensitive dynamics, a jumping story, a distorted signal, random-access editing and leaping thought.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在否认同一条直路：弯折的曲线、断掉的比例、更高次项、敏感的动态、跳跃的故事、失真的信号、随机访问的剪辑，以及跳跃的思路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that refuses to stay straight, bending further the more it is pushed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条不肯保持笔直的线，越推越弯。

branches.en: LEAVING THE STRAIGHT PATH: a curve, a broken ratio and a leap of thought all refuse to advance in equal steps.
branches.cn: 离开直路：曲线、断掉的比例与跳跃的思路，都拒绝按等步长前进。

branches.en: THE ALGEBRA OF BENDS: squared and multiplied terms are what make a line impossible.
branches.cn: 弯折的代数：平方项与乘积项使直线解不再存在。

branches.en: FEEDBACK GROWS: when output returns as input, tiny differences can expand beyond prediction.
branches.cn: 反馈放大：输出回到输入后，微小差异可能扩张到无法预测。

branches.en: JUMPING ORDER: flashbacks and random-access editing both break a single forward sequence.
branches.cn: 跳跃的顺序：倒叙与随机访问剪辑都打破了单一的向前顺序。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL BENDS: clipping destroys the one-to-one match between input and output.
branches.cn: 信号弯折：削顶破坏了输入与输出的一一对应。

intro.en: Nonlinear is an English compound: a Latin negative particle attached to an adjective that Latin built from a noun.
intro.cn: nonlinear 是英语复合词：拉丁否定小品词加一个由拉丁名词构成的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Non- 'not' is Latin in origin but freely used in English; linea and linearis supply the line, while non- has no noun family of its own.
latinIntro.cn: non-「不」源自拉丁，却在英语里自由使用；linea 与 linearis 提供「线」，而 non- 本身没有名词家族。

items.example: Non- simply denies the adjective that follows.
items.exampleCN: non- 只是否定后面那个形容词。

items.example: The Latin noun supplies the geometric core.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词提供几何核心。

items.example: Latin built the adjective; English later negated it.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语造出形容词，英语后来才加否定。

items.example: The positive adjective is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 肯定形式的形容词是复合词的基底。

items.example: The response turned nonlinear at high load.
items.exampleCN: 高负载下响应变成非线性。

items.example: Engineers measure nonlinearity in decibels.
items.exampleCN: 工程师用分贝衡量非线性程度。

items.meaning: to make linear, often as an approximation
items.meaningCN: 使线性化，常作近似处理
items.example: They linearize the curve near the operating point.
items.exampleCN: 他们在工作点附近把曲线线性化。

items.example: The linearization holds only over a small range.
items.exampleCN: 这种线性化只在很小范围内成立。

definition_zh: 可爱的；讨人喜欢的；惹人怜爱的
definition_en: so lovable or charming that people want to hold, protect, or admire the person or thing
core_image: 让人忍不住想伸手抱一下的小东西
scene: 沙发旁，小狗把头搁在孩子的膝盖上，眼睛一眨一眨地看人。 The puppy looked so adorable that everyone stopped to watch.
sceneCN: 这里 adorable 是「可爱的」（第 1 个义项：外貌或举止惹人喜爱）；句意为那只小狗看起来太可爱了，所有人都停下来看。图中可辨识物件：沙发、膝盖、小狗的项圈。

pos.zh: 可爱的；讨人喜欢的；值得爱慕的

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「爱慕；喜爱；敬拜」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「爱慕；敬拜」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「可爱地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「可爱；惹人喜爱」

senses.title: Cute and lovable
senses.definition: so cute or charming in appearance or manner that people feel affection at once
senses.definitionCN: 外貌或举止非常可爱、讨喜，让人立刻生出喜爱
senses.example: The baby's first smile was utterly adorable.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的第一个笑容可爱极了。
senses.why: The word once meant worthy of worship; the affection of worship has been scaled down to the affection of a passing smile.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本意为「值得敬拜」；敬拜的深情被缩小成了对一个微笑的喜爱。

senses.title: Charming in personality
senses.definition: pleasing in character, especially in a warm and harmless way
senses.definitionCN: 性格上令人愉快，尤其是一种温暖而无害的方式
senses.example: He is an adorable old man who remembers every neighbour's name.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位讨人喜欢的老人，记得每位邻居的名字。
senses.why: When affection moves from the face to the person, adorable describes a temperament rather than a look.
senses.whyCN: 当喜爱从脸孔移到整个人，adorable 描述的便是性情而不是长相。

senses.title: Worthy of adoration
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, deserving deep love or reverence
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，值得深切爱慕或敬重
senses.example: The old hymn calls the saint adorable above all others.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的赞美诗称这位圣徒在众人之上，值得敬拜。
senses.why: This is the word's oldest sense kept intact: what deserves adoration, not merely a hug.
senses.whyCN: 这是词最古老的一层，完整保留：值得敬拜，而不只是值得一个拥抱。

senses.title: Endearing, of small creatures
senses.titleCN: 惹人怜爱的（小动物、婴儿）
senses.definition: used of small animals, babies, or small things in a way that invites care and protection
senses.definitionCN: 用于小动物、婴儿或小物件，带有想照顾、想保护的意味
senses.example: The kitten had an adorable way of falling asleep mid-step.
senses.exampleCN: 那只小猫走到一半就睡着的样子很惹人怜爱。
senses.why: Smallness and helplessness pull the word toward tenderness: the object is not only pretty but in need of care.
senses.whyCN: 幼小与无助把词拉向温柔：对象不只是好看，还需要被照顾。

senses.title: Ironic: absurdly charming
senses.definition: used ironically of something childish, awkward, or unreasonable, as if it were charming
senses.definitionCN: 反讽地用于幼稚、别扭或不合理的事物，仿佛它们很迷人
senses.example: He offered the most adorable excuse for missing the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他为错过截止日期给出了一个荒唐得好笑的借口。
senses.why: Many fond words can be turned against their object; calling a bad excuse adorable means it is too childish to be taken seriously.
senses.whyCN: 许多亲昵的词都能反转来用；说一个糟糕的借口 adorable，意思是它幼稚到无法当真。

senses.title: In the speech of children and adults to children
senses.titleCN: 儿童用语里的「太可爱了」
senses.definition: a frequent exclamation in talk addressed to or about children and pets
senses.definitionCN: 在面向儿童或谈论儿童、宠物时常用的感叹说法
senses.example: Look at his tiny boots. Adorable!
senses.exampleCN: 看他那双小靴子。太可爱了！
senses.why: A word used constantly around children becomes part of that register, a quick signal of warm approval.
senses.whyCN: 一个总在孩子身边使用的词，会进入那个语域，成为温暖赞许的快速信号。

senses.title: The archaic religious sense
senses.definition: in older religious writing, describing what is worthy of worship and divine honour
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的宗教文本中，描述值得敬拜与神圣尊崇者
senses.example: The prayer addresses the adorable name with reverence.
senses.exampleCN: 祷词以敬畏之心称呼那个值得敬拜的名。
senses.why: Adore began as a verb of prayer; the adjective kept a religious sense long after everyday speech turned it toward cuteness.
senses.whyCN: adore 原本是祈祷的动词；日常语把它转向「可爱」很久之后，形容词仍保留着宗教义。

senses.title: An affectionate form of address
senses.definition: used as a tender way of addressing a loved person, especially a child
senses.definitionCN: 用作称呼所爱之人的亲昵说法，尤用于孩子
senses.example: Come here, my adorable one, and let me see that bruise.
senses.exampleCN: 过来，我的小可爱，让我看看那块淤青。
senses.why: A descriptive adjective can become a name when affection is spoken directly to the person.
senses.whyCN: 当喜爱直接对着那个人说出时，描述性的形容词就成了称呼。

intro.en: Adorable comes from a Latin verb of prayer, and its meaning slid from worship to affection without losing the intensity.
intro.cn: adorable 来自一个表示「祈祷」的拉丁动词，它的意义从敬拜滑向喜爱，却没有丢掉那份强度。

items.en: The speaking root is often connected with *or-, 'to speak', but the wider reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个「说话」词根常与 *or-「说」相联系，但更广的构拟并不确定。

items.en: Orare meant 'to speak, plead, pray', and it also gives oral, orator and oracle.
items.cn: orare 意为「说话、恳求、祈祷」，它还给出 oral、orator 与 oracle。

items.en: Ad plus orare formed adorare, 'to speak to, pray to, worship'. The prefix turns speech toward its object.
items.cn: ad 与 orare 构成 adorare，意为「对……说话、向……祈祷、敬拜」。前缀把说话指向对象。

items.en: Adorabilis meant 'worthy of adoration'; the suffix -abilis marks what deserves the action.
items.cn: adorabilis 意为「值得敬拜的」；后缀 -abilis 标记值得承受这一动作者。

items.en: Old French and later English kept the religious sense first, applying the word to persons and things worthy of reverence.
items.cn: 古法语与后来的英语先保留宗教义，用它形容值得敬重的人与物。

items.en: The modern 'cute' sense is a later softening: what is loved intensely comes to be called adorable in everyday affection.
items.cn: 现代「可爱」义是后来软化的结果：被深深喜爱的东西在日常亲昵里被称为 adorable。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin prayer verb; the near-meaning group gathers praise words for charm and cuteness, which differ in intensity and in how childish they sound.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「祈祷」动词构成的词；近义组收称赞迷人、可爱的词，彼此在强度与孩子气程度上不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to love intensely or, in older use, to worship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「深爱」，旧时也指「敬拜」。

entries.definition: The noun for deep love or worship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爱慕；敬拜」。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a look or manner full of love.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述充满爱意的目光或举止。

entries.definition: Attractive in a pretty or endearing way, the most everyday word for the same impression.
entries.definitionCN: 以漂亮或惹人喜爱的方式吸引人，是表达同一印象最日常的词。

entries.definition: Deserving love because of character rather than appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 因性格而非外貌而值得被爱，比 adorable 更重心性。

entries.definition: Pleasing and attractive in a social way, often of manner rather than looks.
entries.definitionCN: 在社交上令人愉快、有吸引力，多指举止而非长相。

entries.definition: Kind and pleasing in a gentle, unassuming way.
entries.definitionCN: 温和、不张扬地令人愉快。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin prayer root and the phrases the adjective actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「祈祷」词根，以及这个形容词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: orare means to pray: adore began as worship, and adorable began as worthy of worship.
normal.cn: orare 意为「祈祷」：adore 起初是敬拜，adorable 起初是「值得敬拜」。

normal.en: The same root gives oral and orator, both about speaking.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 oral 与 orator，两者都与说话有关。

normal.en: Adorable is the adjective, adorably the adverb, adorableness the noun.
normal.cn: adorable 是形容词，adorably 是副词，adorableness 是名词。

normal.en: Look adorable and absolutely adorable are the everyday intensifiers.
normal.cn: look adorable 与 absolutely adorable 是日常的搭配与强调。

normal.en: Used of a bad excuse, adorable turns ironic and means childish.
normal.cn: 用在糟糕的借口上，adorable 转为反讽，意思是幼稚。

abstract.en: Picture a very old word kneeling in prayer, then standing up to tickle a puppy.
abstract.cn: 想象一个很古老的词先跪着祈祷，然后站起来去逗小狗。

abstract.en: The intensity never left: we still say adorable when affection is stronger than reason.
abstract.cn: 那份强度从未离开：当喜爱超过理智时，我们仍说 adorable。

abstract.en: Anything small and defenseless borrows the word, and anything absurd can borrow it as a joke.
abstract.cn: 任何幼小无助的东西都能借走这个词，任何荒唐的东西也能借它来开玩笑。

examples.en: Their new puppy is absolutely adorable.
examples.cn: 他们新养的小狗可爱极了。

examples.en: She has an adorable habit of humming while she works.
examples.cn: 她工作时哼歌的习惯很讨人喜欢。

examples.en: The old hymn still calls the saint adorable.
examples.cn: 那首古老的赞美诗仍称这位圣徒值得敬拜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿多勒伯」——阿多伸手想抱：可爱得让人爱

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ orare（说话、祈祷）构成 adorare「向……祈祷、敬拜」，加 -abilis「值得……的」构成 adorabilis，本义「值得敬拜的」，现代日常语中软化为「可爱的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adorable run from plain cuteness through charm, formal reverence, tender smallness, irony, child talk, the archaic religious sense and a lover's form of address.
sensesIntro.cn: adorable 的八个义项从单纯的可爱，经讨喜的性格、正式的敬慕、惹人怜爱的幼小、反讽、儿童用语、古老的宗教义，一直到亲昵的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something small looks up at you and your hand reaches out before you decide to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小东西抬头看你，你的手在决定之前就已经伸出去了。

branches.en: THE WORSHIP LINE: the oldest layer keeps the word pointed at what deserves reverence.
branches.cn: 敬拜线：最古老的一层让这个词仍指向值得敬重之物。

branches.en: THE AFFECTION LINE: reverence scaled down becomes warm liking of a face or a character.
branches.cn: 喜爱线：敬重被缩小，成了对一张脸或一种性情的温暖喜欢。

branches.en: THE TENDERNESS LINE: smallness and helplessness invite care and protection.
branches.cn: 温柔线：幼小与无助唤起照顾与保护。

branches.en: THE IRONY LINE: the same fond word can mock what is childish or absurd.
branches.cn: 反讽线：同一个亲昵的词可以嘲弄幼稚或荒唐之物。

branches.en: THE SPEECH LINE: constant use around children turns the adjective into an exclamation and a pet name.
branches.cn: 言语线：在孩子身边的频繁使用，把这个形容词变成感叹与昵称。

intro.en: Adorable is a Latin prefix and prayer verb plus the suffix -able; English adds -ly and -ness, and the verb adore stands at the base.
intro.cn: adorable 由拉丁语前缀、祈祷动词与后缀 -able 构成；英语再加 -ly 与 -ness，动词 adore 是它的基础。

latinIntro.en: Orare, adorare and adorabilis are all recorded in Latin, so the core is documented rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: orare、adorare 与 adorabilis 在拉丁语中都有记录，核心部分有文献可查，不属重构。

items.exampleCN: 它把说话指向被称呼者。

items.example: It is the speaking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「说话」词根。

items.example: The compound is the source of adore.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是 adore 的来源。

items.example: It forms adorabilis.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adorabilis。

items.example: It forms adorable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adorable。

items.example: It forms adorably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adorably。

items.example: It forms adorableness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adorableness。

items.example: It forms adoration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adoration。

由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「爱慕；敬拜」

definition_zh: 立法的；立法机关的；有立法权的；由立法设立的
definition_en: relating to the making of laws or to the body that makes them
core_image: 一间半圆形的议事厅，座位上标着选区名，中央的书记员正在点票
scene: 修稿一直改到表决前一小时，主席仍要求先算清票数。 The legislative committee rewrote the clause before the final vote.
sceneCN: 这里 legislative 指属于立法机关及其程序的（第 1 个义项：与立法机关有关）；句意为立法委员会在最终表决前重写了该条款。

pos.zh: 立法的；立法机关的；有立法权的

derivatives.zh: 立法；法规（legislate + -ion「行为或结果」，由属性转指其所指的过程与产物）
立法机关（legislate + -ure「机构」，由属性转指持有它的机关）
立法者（legislate + -or「行事者」，由属性转指人）
立法（由 legislative 的词干逆构，由属性转指行为）

senses.title: Of the law-making body
senses.definition: belonging to the assembly that makes laws, as opposed to the executive or the courts
senses.definitionCN: 属于制定法律的议会，与行政或法院相对
senses.example: The legislative calendar leaves little room for debate.
senses.exampleCN: 立法日程几乎没给辩论留空间。
senses.why: the suffix -ive marks a body's characteristic function, so the adjective names the branch by what it does.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 标示某机构特有的职能，因此形容词按它做什么来命名这一分支。

senses.title: Holding the power to make law
senses.definition: possessing authority to enact binding law
senses.definitionCN: 持有颁行有约束力法律的权威
senses.example: Legislative power cannot be delegated without limits.
senses.exampleCN: 立法权不能无限制地授出。
senses.why: power is what separates law-making from advising, so the adjective attaches to authority itself.
senses.whyCN: 权力把立法与建议区分开，因此形容词也直接接在权威上。

senses.title: Of the procedure
senses.definition: concerning the steps of reading, amending and voting on a bill
senses.definitionCN: 关于议案的宣读、修正与表决步骤
senses.example: A legislative deadlock can outlast a session.
senses.exampleCN: 立法僵局可以跨会期延续。
senses.why: procedure is the visible part of law-making, so the adjective routinely describes it.
senses.whyCN: 程序是立法最可见的部分，因此形容词经常描述它。

senses.title: Created by statute
senses.definition: established by an act of a legislature rather than by administrative decision
senses.definitionCN: 由立法机关的法令、而非行政决定设立
senses.example: The ombudsman is a legislative creation, not a ministerial one.
senses.exampleCN: 监察专员是立法设立的，而非部长设立的。
senses.why: the adjective can mark origin, telling us which kind of authority brought a body into being.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可标示来源，说明是哪一类权威使某机构得以成立。

senses.title: Law-making in character
senses.definition: having the character of law-making even outside a parliament, as with a treaty clause
senses.definitionCN: 即使不在议会之内，也带立法性质，如条约条款
senses.example: The council's vote had a legislative effect on the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会的投票对整个地区产生了立法效果。
senses.why: the adjective can describe an effect rather than a body, since making binding rules is what defines it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可描述效果而非机构，因为「制定有约束力的规则」才是它的定义特征。

senses.title: Separated from executive and judicial
senses.definition: naming one of the three functions of government in the doctrine of separation of powers
senses.definitionCN: 在三权分立学说中指政府三大职能之一
senses.example: Legislative independence was the point of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 立法独立正是这场改革的要点。
senses.why: the modern sense is defined by contrast: legislative is whatever the other two branches are not.
senses.whyCN: 现代义靠对照定义：立法者就是另外两支所不是的那个。

senses.title: Of members or elections
senses.titleCN: 立法机关成员的、议员选举的
senses.definition: concerning the members of a legislature or the elections that seat them
senses.definitionCN: 关于立法机关成员或使其当选的选举
senses.example: Legislative elections were moved up by six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 立法机关选举提前了六周。
senses.why: metonymy lets the branch stand for the people in it, a very common journalistic shorthand.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让这一分支代表其中的人，是新闻语体极常见的简称。

senses.title: Legislative history
senses.titleCN: 立法沿革资料（用于解释法条）
senses.definition: the record of debates, drafts and reports used by courts to interpret a statute
senses.definitionCN: 法院解释法条时所用的辩论、草案与报告记录
senses.example: Judges read the legislative record before ruling on intent.
senses.exampleCN: 法官在裁定立法意图之前先读立法记录。
senses.why: English gives this technical sense to the adjective because the material belongs to the law-making stage.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个技术义交给形容词，因为该材料属于立法阶段。

intro.en: Legislative is the adjective of legislation, from Latin lex 'law' and latus 'carried', the participle of ferre. The English adjective appears in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislative 是 legislation 的形容词，来自拉丁 lex「法」与 latus「被搬运的」，后者是 ferre 的分词。英语形容词见于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex 'law' has no established deeper origin; the old suggestion of a link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis only.
items.cn: lex「法」的更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」有关的旧说仅为假说。

items.en: Latus is the suppletive participle of ferre 'to carry'; legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly.
items.cn: latus 是 ferre「搬运」的异干互补分词；legis latio 指把议案带到大会之前。

items.en: Legislatio generalized the phrase to law-making, and its adjective legislativus described what belongs to that function.
items.cn: legislatio 把这一说法一般化为立法，其形容词 legislativus 描述属于该职能之物。

items.en: French législatif passed into English in the seventeenth century, at first in writing on the separation of powers.
items.cn: 法语 législatif 在 17 世纪进入英语，最初见于论三权分立的著述。

items.en: With the spread of written constitutions the adjective became a fixed label for one branch, always defined against the executive and the courts.
items.cn: 随着成文宪法的传播，这个形容词成为某一分支的固定标签，总在与行政、法院的对照中被定义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not exactly dated, and the origin of lex remains unsettled, so older forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the legisl- stem; group two holds adjectives of government functions.
note.cn: 第一组共享 legisl- 词干；第二组是政府各职能的形容词。

entries.definition: The act or the body of laws; the adjective only describes what belongs to that act.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或法律总体；形容词只描述属于该行为之物。

entries.definition: The body that legislates; a legislative committee belongs to it rather than being it.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的机构；立法委员会属于它，而不等于它。

entries.definition: From legitimus 'lawful'; it shares the lex root but means permitted, not legislative.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legitimus「合法的」；共享 lex 词根，却意为获准的，而非立法的。

entries.definition: A member who makes law; the adjective would describe the member's work, not the member.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员；形容词描述其工作，而非其本人。

entries.definition: Of a parliament's rules and manners; legislative concerns law-making power, which is narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会的规则与礼仪；legislative 关注立法权，范围更窄。

entries.definition: Created or required by a particular act; legislative describes the function rather than the binding force.
entries.definitionCN: 由某部法令创设或要求；legislative 描述职能，而非约束力。

entries.definition: Of the branch that carries out policy; it is defined by contrast with legislative and judicial.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行政策的分支；它与立法、司法相对而被定义。

entries.definition: The everyday compound for the same idea; legislative is its formal, constitutional counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意思的日常复合词；legislative 是其正式、宪制性的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio 'bringing of a law' plus -ive: having the character of that bringing.
normal.cn: legis latio「把法带来」加 -ive：带有那种「带来」的性质。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branch: legislative power, legislative committee, legislative agenda.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一分支：立法权、立法委员会、立法议程。

normal.en: Three adjectives divide the state: legislative, executive, judicial.
normal.cn: 三个形容词把国家切开：立法的、行政的、司法的。

normal.en: The technical phrase legislative history sends courts back to the debates.
normal.cn: 术语 legislative history 把法院送回辩论记录。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the only thing made is sentences that bind people outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，里面唯一制造的东西是能约束屋外之人的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall that later requires thousands of hands to obey.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里举起的一只手，日后要成千上万只手服从。

abstract.en: Picture three pillars, and the left one is always described by what the other two are not.
abstract.cn: 想象三根柱子，左边那根总是靠另外两根「不是什么」来描述。

examples.en: The legislative branch cannot enforce its own statutes.
examples.cn: 立法分支无法自己执行其法令。

examples.en: A legislative fix would take a full session.
examples.cn: 用立法方式修补需要整整一个会期。

examples.en: The court consulted the legislative record before ruling.
examples.cn: 法院在裁定前查考了立法记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lat（带来）+ ive（……的）＝ 把法带来的那一支；记「只造规则，不管执行」。

root: 拉丁 lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latus「被搬运的」（ferre「搬运」的分词）+ 形容词后缀 -ive。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one function from outside: the body that makes law, the power it holds, its procedure, what it creates, its effect elsewhere, its place in the division of powers, its members, and the record it leaves for courts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从外部描述同一职能：制定法律的机关、它持有的权力、它的程序、它创设之物、它在别处的效果、它在分权中的位置、它的成员，以及它留给法院的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand in a chamber that turns a sentence into a rule binding those outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：议事厅里举起的一只手，把一句话变成约束厅外之人的规则。

branches.en: BODY AND POWER: the assembly, and the authority that makes its words binding.
branches.cn: 机关与权力：议会，以及使其言语有约束力的权威。

branches.en: PROCEDURE AND PRODUCT: the steps, then the bodies and rules those steps create.
branches.cn: 程序与产物：先是步骤，再是这些步骤所创设的机构与规则。

branches.en: EFFECT WITHOUT A CHAMBER: legislative quality can attach to a treaty or a council vote.
branches.cn: 无厅之效：立法性质也可附在条约或委员会表决上。

branches.en: DEFINED BY CONTRAST: the branch is what the executive and the courts are not.
branches.cn: 靠对照定义：这一分支就是行政与法院所不是的。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PAPER: the members elected, and the record they leave behind.
branches.cn: 人与纸：选出的成员，以及他们留下的记录。

intro.en: Legislative is built from a Latin law noun, a Latin participle and an English adjective suffix, so each part can be read alone.
intro.cn: legislative 由拉丁「法」名词、拉丁分词与英语形容词后缀构成，每一部分都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Lex gives legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre give transfer, refer, relate and translate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate、translate。

items.example: Lex underlies legal and legitimate.
items.exampleCN: lex 支撑 legal 与 legitimate。

items.example: The participle supplies the second half of legislation.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了 legislation 的后半。

items.meaning: tending to, having the character of
items.example: The suffix turns a function into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一种职能变成形容词。

items.example: Only the chamber may legislate here.
items.exampleCN: 此处只有该院可以立法。

items.example: The legislative session opened late.
items.exampleCN: 立法会期开得晚。

items.example: Legislation followed the inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 调查之后才有立法。

items.example: The legislature met for six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 立法机关开了六周会。

items.example: The issue was addressed legislatively.
items.exampleCN: 该问题是以立法方式处理的。

items.example: One legislator held the floor for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 一位议员占了一个小时的发言。

definition_zh: 别名；化名；又名
definition_en: a false or alternative name used by someone, or the word meaning 'otherwise called'
core_image: 两本护照同一张脸：名字换了一个，人还是那个人
scene: 通缉令上写着他的真名，后面还跟着另一个名字。 The spy checked into the hotel under an alias.
sceneCN: 这里 alias 是「化名、别名」（第 1 个义项：使用假名或另一个名字）；句意是间谍用化名登记入住酒店。

pos.zh: 别名；化名
又名；亦称

derivatives.zh: alias 加 -ed 构成（技术用语），义为「使用别名的；被重命名的」
同根派生词，源自同一拉丁词根 alius，义为「使疏远；使 alienated」
同根近亲词，源自拉丁「在别处」，义为「不在场证明；借口」

senses.title: A false or assumed name
senses.definition: a name someone uses to hide their real identity
senses.definitionCN: 为隐瞒真实身分而使用的名字
senses.example: The fugitive lived for years under an alias.
senses.exampleCN: 这名逃犯用化名生活了多年。
senses.why: Latin alias means 'at another time, otherwise': the name belongs to the same person at another time or in another role.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alias 意为「在别的时候、换个说法」：这个名字属于同一个人的另一时刻或另一身分。

senses.title: An alternative name or label
senses.definition: another name by which a person or thing is also known, neutral in tone
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物另外的称呼，语气中性
senses.example: Markdown, alias 'md', is the format of these files.
senses.exampleCN: Markdown，又名 md，是这些文件的格式。
senses.why: When no deception is intended, the same 'otherwise called' sense simply names a second label.
senses.whyCN: 当不含欺瞒意图时，同样的「亦可称」之义只表示第二种称呼。

intro.en: A Latin adverb meaning 'otherwise, at another time', turned by legal Latin into a name marker.
intro.cn: 一个意为「否则、在别时」的拉丁副词，经法律拉丁语转变为标记别名的用词。

items.en: A reconstructed root *h₂el- expressed 'beyond, other', also seen in alien and else.
items.cn: 重构词根 *h₂el- 表示「在另一边、别的」，也见于 alien 与 else。

items.en: alias meant 'at another time, otherwise', an ordinary adverb of difference.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alias 意为「在别时、否则」，是表示差异的普通副词。

items.en: Scribes wrote 'John Smith alias John Brown' to link two names of one person.
items.cn: 文书用 John Smith alias John Brown 标明同一人的两个名字。

items.en: The marker entered English both as the adverb 'otherwise called' and as a noun for a false name.
items.cn: 16 世纪该词进入英语，既作「又名」的副词，也作「化名」的名词。

items.en: Today computing borrows it for alternative file or command names.
items.cn: 现代计算机术语借用它指文件或命令的别名。

note.en: The first group gathers the Latin 'other' family and a look-alike; the second gathers words for names.
note.cn: 第一组收拉丁语「别的」词族与一个形近词；第二组收表示「名字」的词。

entries.definition: elsewhere; a claim of being elsewhere, hence an excuse
entries.definitionCN: 不在场证明；借口

entries.definition: belonging to another; a foreigner
entries.definitionCN: 外国的；外星人

entries.definition: to make someone feel estranged
entries.definitionCN: 使疏远

entries.definition: in computing, one name pointing to the same stored item
entries.definitionCN: （计算机）别名现象；指向同一存储项

entries.definition: a made-up name, especially for writers
entries.definitionCN: 假名；笔名

entries.definition: an assumed name, originally for fighters
entries.definitionCN: 化名；原指战士所用假名

entries.definition: a name taken on deliberately, like an alias
entries.definitionCN: 假名；刻意采用的名字

entries.definition: a writer's alternative name
entries.definitionCN: 笔名

entries.definition: an informal, familiar name given in addition to the real one
entries.definitionCN: 绰号；昵称

normalIntro.en: Latin alias, 'otherwise': the same person, another name.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alias 意为「换个说法」：同一个人，另一个名字。

normal.en: under an alias is the fixed phrase for using one.
normal.cn: 使用化名的固定说法是 under an alias。

normal.en: Alien, alibi, alias all hold the Latin 'other'.
normal.cn: alien、alibi、alias 都藏着拉丁语的「别的」。

normal.en: Spies and criminals use aliases; writers use pseudonyms.
normal.cn: 间谍和罪犯用化名，作家用笔名。

normal.en: In terminals, alias sets a shortcut name for a command.
normal.cn: 在终端里，alias 为命令设置快捷名。

normal.en: Plural: one alias, two aliases.
normal.cn: 复数：一个 alias，两个 aliases。

abstract.en: Picture one face behind two different hotel registers.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张脸出现在两本不同的酒店登记簿上。

abstract.en: See a name being peeled off like a sticker, a new one pressed on.
abstract.cn: 想象名字像贴纸一样被揭下，再贴上一张新的。

abstract.en: Imagine a message that arrives signed with two names joined by 'alias'.
abstract.cn: 想象一封署名处写着两个名字、中间夹着 alias 的信。

examples.en: She wrote three novels under an alias.
examples.cn: 她用笔名写了三部小说。

examples.en: The card went by the alias 'the Duchess'.
examples.cn: 这名骗子化名「公爵夫人」行骗。

examples.en: Set an alias for that long command to save typing.
examples.cn: 给那条长命令设个别名，省得每次都打全。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱理啊死」——换了名字装不认识，你爱理不理，他却假装不认识你。

root: 拉丁语副词 alias「在别时、否则」来自 alius「别的」（词根可溯至重构形式 *h₂el-），法律文书用它连接同一人的两个名字，16 世纪进入英语；同族词有 alien、alibi、alienate。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses divide the 'otherwise' by intent: a name worn to hide, or simply a second name on record.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项按意图区分「亦可称」：一个是用来隐匿身分的名字，一个只是备案的第二称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one face, two names on two registers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸，两本登记簿上两个名字。

branches.en: a fugitive signing a stranger's name
branches.cn: 逃犯签下一个陌生人的名字

branches.en: a spy's passport that lies about everything but the face
branches.cn: 除了脸以外通篇是假的间谍护照

branches.en: a file known to the system by a shorter label
branches.cn: 系统里用更短标签称呼的文件

branches.en: a city listed under an older spelling
branches.cn: 以旧拼写备案的城市名

branches.en: the same second name, with or without a secret behind it
branches.cn: 同一个别名，背后或有秘密，或无秘密

intro.en: A Latin root for 'other' wearing the adverb ending alias, plus its English offspring.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「别的」词根带上副词词尾 alias，加上它在英语中的后代。

latinIntro.en: alius and alias are recorded Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: alius 与 alias 都是有记录的拉丁形态。

items.exampleCN: 一个……另一个
