definition_zh: 学术上；在学业方面；从学术角度看
definition_en: in relation to academic study, or in a way that concerns school and university learning
core_image: 公告栏把毕业生分成几档，最高一栏写着进入研究型大学的人数
scene: 县中学的公告栏上，毕业生被分成几档，最高一栏写着进入研究型大学的人数。 She was academically strong but struggled in the workshop.
sceneCN: 这里 academically 指「在学业与学术表现方面」（第 1 个义项：就学业而言）；句意为她在学业上很强，但在车间里却吃力。可辨识物件：公告栏、排名表、红笔标记、车间工具。

pos.zh: 学术上；在学业方面；从学术角度看

derivatives.zh: 学术的；大学教师
学术界
学院；学会
学院主义

senses.title: In terms of study
senses.definition: with respect to school or university learning rather than practical or social matters
senses.definitionCN: 就中小学或大学的学习而言，而非实务或社交方面
senses.example: She was academically strong but struggled in the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学业上很强，但在车间里却吃力。
senses.why: The adverb marks the domain being judged, so it sets study apart from other kinds of ability.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标出被评判的领域，从而把学业与其他能力区分开。

senses.title: Performing well in study
senses.definition: in a way that shows high achievement in academic subjects
senses.definitionCN: 在学科成绩上显出高水平
senses.example: The scholarship is awarded to academically outstanding students.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金颁给学业出众的学生。
senses.why: Achievement needs a measure, and the adverb supplies the academic yardstick.
senses.whyCN: 成绩需要一把尺，这个副词提供的正是学业这把尺。

senses.title: As a matter of school orientation
senses.definition: in a way that treats academic subjects as the main purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把学科学习当作主要目的的做法
senses.example: The school is academically oriented but weak in sport.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以学业为重，体育却薄弱。
senses.why: Institutions choose what to emphasise, and the adverb names the emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 学校会选择强调什么，这个副词命名的就是那种强调。

senses.title: By academic standards
senses.definition: judged against the rigour expected in scholarship
senses.definitionCN: 按照学术研究应有的严格程度来评判
senses.example: The programme is academically rigorous.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目学术要求严格。
senses.why: Standards differ by field, and the adverb anchors the judgement in academic expectations.
senses.whyCN: 标准因领域而异，这个副词把判断锚定在学术期待上。

senses.title: Recognised in academic terms
senses.definition: validated by scholarly criteria rather than commercial or popular ones
senses.definitionCN: 按学术标准而非商业或大众标准获得认可
senses.example: The qualification is academically recognised abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这一资格在国外获得学术承认。
senses.why: Recognition can come from several quarters, and the adverb says which one counts.
senses.whyCN: 认可可以来自多方，这个副词说明哪一方算数。

senses.title: At an academic disadvantage
senses.titleCN: 在学业条件上处于劣势
senses.definition: in a way that leaves a student behind in school learning
senses.definitionCN: 在学业学习上使学生处于落后状态
senses.example: Rural pupils were academically disadvantaged by the closures.
senses.exampleCN: 学校关闭使农村学生在学业上处于劣势。
senses.why: Gaps are measured in learning, so disadvantage is often described with this adverb.
senses.whyCN: 差距是以学习来衡量的，因此劣势常用这个副词来描述。

senses.title: Speaking academically
senses.definition: in the manner of academic discussion, with definitions and evidence
senses.definitionCN: 以学术讨论的方式，带定义与证据
senses.example: Academically speaking, the two terms are not interchangeable.
senses.exampleCN: 从学术角度说，这两个术语不能互换。
senses.why: The adverb can also frame a whole statement as scholarly rather than casual.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词也能把整句话框定为学术性的，而非随意的。

senses.title: Pursuing an academic path
senses.definition: in a direction that leads towards research and university teaching
senses.definitionCN: 朝着研究与大学教学发展的方向
senses.example: He was academically inclined from an early age.
senses.exampleCN: 他从小就偏向学术。
senses.why: A career choice can be academic, and the adverb describes the inclination.
senses.whyCN: 职业选择也可以是学术性的，这个副词描述的正是那种倾向。

intro.en: Academically is the adverb of academic, which descends from the name of Plato's school in Athens. The dates are approximate.
intro.cn: academically 是表示「学术的」那个形容词的副词形式，而该形容词源自雅典柏拉图学园的名字。年代均为约数。

items.en: The grove outside Athens where Plato taught was named after a local hero; the hero's own name is of uncertain origin and is marked as source uncertain.
items.cn: 柏拉图授课的雅典郊外园林以一位当地英雄命名；这位英雄名字本身的来源不确定，标为来源不确定。

items.en: Latin took the place name as a noun for the school and its followers, and the word kept the philosophical setting.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个地名用作名词，指该学园及其追随者，词义保留着哲学场景。

items.en: The adjective meant 'of the Academy', and it described both the place and the kind of discussion held there.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「学园的」，既描述地点，也描述在那里进行的那类讨论。

items.en: English adopted the adjective for things belonging to schools of higher learning, and later for scholarly subjects in general.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，指属于高等学府的事物，后来泛指学术科目。

items.en: Adding the ordinary adverb ending produced a word for judging something by academic standards.
items.cn: 加上普通的副词词尾，就得到按学术标准评判某事的词。

items.en: Source uncertain (hero's name): the origin of the name behind the place is not established, so any deeper etymology is a hypothesis rather than a result.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英雄之名）：该地名背后那个人名的来源未得证明，任何更深的词源都只是假说，而非结论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same school name; group two holds adverbs of learning that come from other roots.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一学园名称的形式；第二组是来自其他词根、表示学习的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective describes what belongs to study; the adverb describes how something is done or judged.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词描述属于学习的事物；副词描述某事如何被做或被评判。

entries.definition: The noun for the academic world; it names the place or community, not the manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指学术界的名词；它命名场所或群体，而非方式。

entries.definition: A school or learned society; the word keeps the original institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 学校或学术团体；这个词保留着原本的机构义。

entries.definition: From a Greek word for a teacher, but with a negative tone; it means in an overly bookish way.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语中表示教师的词，但带贬义；意为过于拘泥书本地。

entries.definition: In terms of the education system as a whole; it is broader than academically.
entries.definitionCN: 就整个教育制度而言；比 academically 更宽。

entries.definition: In relation to formal schooling and examinations; it sounds older and narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 就正式学校教育与考试而言；听起来更旧、更窄。

entries.definition: In terms of thinking and reasoning ability, whether or not a school is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 就思考与推理能力而言，未必涉及学校。

entries.definition: In terms of doing and use; it is the usual contrast to academically.
entries.definitionCN: 就动手与实际运用而言；常作为 academically 的对照。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the school name at the root, the adverb ending, and the practical contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词根里的学园名称、副词词尾，以及与实务的对照。

normal.en: The root is the name of Plato's school, so anything academically judged is judged by school standards.
normal.cn: 词根是柏拉图学园的名字，因此凡按 academically 评判的，都是按学校标准评判。

normal.en: The ending turns the adjective into a statement about how something is done or measured.
normal.cn: 词尾把形容词变成关于「如何做或如何衡量」的陈述。

normal.en: The usual contrast is practical: strong academically, weak in the workshop.
normal.cn: 最常见的对照是实务：学业强，车间里弱。

normal.en: School phrases carry it: academically gifted, academically oriented, academically disadvantaged.
normal.cn: 学校说法常带着它：学业有天赋、以学业为重、学业处于劣势。

normal.en: The whole Academy family shares the name: academic, academia, academy, academically.
normal.cn: 整个「学园」词族共享这个名字：学术的、学术界、学院、学术上。

abstract.en: Picture a report card read aloud while a toolbox sits untouched.
abstract.cn: 想象有人朗读成绩单，而工具箱一直没被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder leaning against a library shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子靠在图书馆的书架旁。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler marked in grades rather than in centimetres.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子刻的是成绩等级，而不是厘米。

examples.en: The two candidates were academically comparable.
examples.cn: 两位候选人在学业上相当。

examples.en: Academically, the argument is sound but the evidence is thin.
examples.cn: 从学术上说，论证成立，但证据薄弱。

examples.en: The programme is academically demanding and practically useful.
examples.cn: 这个项目学术要求高，也很实用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「学园里那一套」——按学校的标准来评 → 学术上

root: academic（学术的，源自雅典柏拉图学园的地名）+ 英语副词词尾；英语 academically 指在学业方面、按学术标准。该地名背后人名的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question: measured by which standard? The adverb keeps pointing to the school, from plain study through achievement, orientation, rigour, recognition, disadvantage, formal phrasing and career direction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：按哪把尺来衡量？这个副词始终指向学校，从单纯的学习，到成绩、办学方向、严格程度、认可、劣势、正式表述与职业方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked in grades instead of centimetres.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻着成绩等级而非厘米的尺子。

branches.en: THE DOMAIN: the adverb first marks that the judgement concerns study rather than life in general.
branches.cn: 领域：这个副词首先标出判断针对学习，而非一般生活。

branches.en: THE SCALE'S TWO ENDS: the same measure records high achievement and serious disadvantage.
branches.cn: 尺子的两端：同一把尺既记录优异成绩，也记录严重劣势。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION'S CHOICE: a school can emphasise academic work and set its rigour.
branches.cn: 学校的选择：学校可以强调学业，并设定其严格程度。

branches.en: THE STAMP: recognition by academic criteria is a seal from one particular authority.
branches.cn: 印章：按学术标准的认可，是某一个特定权威盖下的章。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND THE PATH: the adverb can frame a sentence or point a career towards research.
branches.cn: 框定与路径：这个副词既能框定一句话，也能把职业指向研究。

intro.en: Academically is a three-piece English word: a borrowed stem, an adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: academically 是三段式英语词：借来的词干、形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is the Greek place name as Latin took it; the endings are the ordinary English adjective and adverb endings.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语所取的希腊地名；词尾是普通的英语形容词与副词词尾。

items.structure: Akademeia (Greek place name, the grove of a hero)
items.example: The place name became the word for a school.
items.exampleCN: 这个地名成了表示学校的词。

items.structure: academia (Latin noun from the place name)
items.example: The noun keeps the institutional sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留机构义。

items.example: Academic standards vary.
items.exampleCN: 学术标准各有不同。

items.example: The ending forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成形容词。

items.example: The ending forms the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成副词。

items.example: The class is academically mixed.
items.exampleCN: 这个班学业水平参差。

items.example: The academy trained painters.
items.exampleCN: 这所学院培养画家。

items.example: The style was attacked as academicism.
items.exampleCN: 这种风格被指为学院主义。

latinEntries.meaning: the Academy; a school of philosophy

definition_zh: 绿洲；（喻）安宁之地；慰藉
definition_en: a place in a desert where water is found and plants grow
core_image: 沙海中央一小片棕榈和水的绿色圆斑，四周全是黄沙
scene: 驼队走了三天，地平线上出现一排棕榈和一片反光的水面。 The caravan rested for two days at the oasis.
sceneCN: 这里 oasis 指「绿洲」（第 1 个义项：沙漠中有水源、能生长植物的地点）；句意为驼队在绿洲休息了两天。

pos.zh: 绿洲；安宁之地；慰藉（可数，希腊式复数 oases）

derivatives.zh: oasis 的希腊式复数（-es 来自希腊 -ες 经拉丁 -es，非派生后缀）→ 绿洲的复数
oasis + town（复合名词，无后缀）→ 建在绿洲上的城镇
oasis + agriculture（复合名词，无后缀）→ 依赖绿洲水源的农业
oasis + ecosystem（复合名词，无后缀）→ 绿洲生态系统
oasis + -like（古英语 -līc，表「像……」的形容词后缀）→ 绿洲般的

senses.title: A watered place in a desert
senses.titleCN: 沙漠绿洲：有水的绿色地点
senses.definition: a place in a desert where ground water reaches the surface and plants can grow
senses.definitionCN: 沙漠中地下水出露、植物得以生长的地方
senses.example: The caravan rested for two days at the oasis.
senses.exampleCN: 驼队在绿洲休息了两天。
senses.why: oasis names a spot defined by contrast: water and green in the middle of dry sand.
senses.whyCN: oasis 命名一个由对比界定的地点：干旱沙地中间的水与绿色。

senses.title: The water source itself
senses.titleCN: 绿洲水源：泉眼与地下水
senses.definition: the spring or well that supplies an oasis
senses.definitionCN: 供养绿洲的泉或井
senses.example: The oasis is fed by a spring that never dries.
senses.exampleCN: 这处绿洲由一眼永不干涸的泉供养。
senses.why: a green spot is made by water reaching the surface, so the word can name the spring that creates it.
senses.whyCN: 绿色地点由到达地表的水造就，因此这个词可以命名造就它的泉。

senses.title: An oasis settlement
senses.titleCN: 绿洲聚落：依水而建的村镇
senses.definition: a village or town built around an oasis
senses.definitionCN: 围绕绿洲建成的村庄或城镇
senses.example: A small oasis grew into a trading town.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小绿洲发展成了贸易城镇。
senses.why: water attracts people, and a settlement grows around the source, so the place-name extends to the village.
senses.whyCN: 水吸引人，聚落围绕水源生长，因此地点之名扩展到村庄。

senses.title: Oasis agriculture
senses.titleCN: 绿洲农业：依靠灌溉的耕作
senses.definition: farming practised on irrigated land within a desert oasis
senses.definitionCN: 在沙漠绿洲内依靠灌溉进行的耕作
senses.example: Oasis agriculture depends on careful water use.
senses.exampleCN: 绿洲农业依赖精打细算的用水。
senses.why: the same water supports irrigation, so the word names the farming system built on it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的水支撑灌溉，因此这个词命名建立在其上的农业体系。

senses.title: The oasis ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 绿洲生态系统：孤立而脆弱的生境
senses.definition: the community of palms, crops and animals supported by an oasis
senses.definitionCN: 由绿洲供养的棕榈、作物与动物群落
senses.example: The oasis ecosystem is isolated by surrounding desert.
senses.exampleCN: 绿洲生态系统被四周沙漠隔离。
senses.why: an isolated watered patch supports a distinct community, which ecology names as an ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: 孤立的有水斑块支撑独特群落，生态学称之为生态系统。

senses.title: A place of calm
senses.titleCN: 比喻：纷扰中的安宁之所
senses.definition: a quiet place or moment that feels protected from surrounding pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在周围压力中显得受保护的安静之处或时刻
senses.example: The library was an oasis of calm in the busy city.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆是繁忙城市中的一片宁静绿洲。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the contrast of dry and green: calm stands out because everything around it is demanding.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「干旱与青绿」的对比：宁静之所以突出，因为四周都在索取。

senses.title: A small source of relief
senses.titleCN: 比喻：稀缺的慰藉与亮点
senses.definition: a small amount of something good in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 困境中少量令人宽慰的好事
senses.example: The good news was an oasis in a week of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 那条好消息是一周失败中的一片绿洲。
senses.why: the contrast of dry and green is transferred from landscape to experience, giving a small good thing the name of a watered place.
senses.whyCN: 干旱与青绿的对比从景观移到经验，使一件小小的好事获得「有水之地」的名字。

senses.title: How an oasis forms
senses.titleCN: 绿洲形成：地下水出露的水文过程
senses.definition: the geological and hydrological process by which water reaches the desert surface
senses.definitionCN: 水到达沙漠表面的地质与水文过程
senses.example: The oasis forms where the aquifer meets a fault.
senses.exampleCN: 绿洲在含水层与断层相接处形成。
senses.why: hydrology asks how the water gets there, so the word also names the process of formation.
senses.whyCN: 水文学追问水如何到达那里，因此这个词也命名形成过程。

intro.en: Oasis came into English through Latin and Greek from an Egyptian word for a watered place in the desert, probably Coptic ouahe. English has used it since the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oasis 经拉丁语与希腊语进入英语，源头是埃及语中指沙漠中水源地的词，可能是科普特语 ouahe。英语自 17 世纪使用。年代均为约数。

items.en: An Egyptian word, transliterated roughly as wahat, named a fertile spot in the desert; the exact vocalisation is reconstructed.
items.cn: 一个埃及语词，转写大致作 wahat，指沙漠中的肥沃地点；确切元音属重构。

items.en: Greek writers used oasis for the watered depressions of the Libyan desert, and the Greek form is the one that reached Europe.
items.cn: 希腊作者用 oasis 指利比亚沙漠中有水的洼地，进入欧洲的正是这个希腊形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun unchanged; English took it from Latin or French in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊名词；英语在 17 世纪从拉丁语或法语借入。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century exploration fixed the modern image of palm trees, a pool and a caravan.
items.cn: 18 与 19 世纪的探险固定了棕榈、水塘与驼队的现代意象。

items.en: By the twentieth century an oasis can be any small area of calm or relief inside a hostile surroundings.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，绿洲可以指敌意环境中的任何一小片安宁或慰藉。

items.en: Source uncertain: the Egyptian-to-Greek transmission and the exact vocalisation are reconstructed, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代存疑）：从埃及语到希腊语的传递与确切元音形式属重构，英语首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds the plural and the look-alikes most often confused with oasis; group two holds the words for watered places and refuges.
note.cn: 第一组是复数形式与最易混淆的形近词；第二组是「有水之处」与「庇护所」的说法。

entries.definition: The plural of oasis, not a separate place; English keeps the Greek -es ending.
entries.definitionCN: oasis 的复数，并非另一个地点；英语保留希腊语 -es 词尾。

entries.definition: An imaginary line about which a body turns; it is shorter and differently stressed.
entries.definitionCN: 物体绕其旋转的假想线；词更短，重音也不同。

entries.definition: A suffix meaning a condition or process, as in osmosis or diagnosis; it is not a noun for a place.
entries.definitionCN: 表示状态或过程的后缀，如 osmosis、diagnosis；它不是地点的名词。

entries.definition: A natural pool where animals drink, usually smaller and less planted than an oasis.
entries.definitionCN: 动物饮水的天然水塘，通常比绿洲小、植被少。

entries.definition: A place where ground water flows naturally to the surface; an oasis may be built around one.
entries.definitionCN: 地下水自然流出地表之处；绿洲可能围绕泉形成。

entries.definition: A place of safety or rest; the metaphorical oasis is a haven of calm.
entries.definitionCN: 安全或休憩之处；比喻的绿洲就是宁静的避风港。

entries.definition: A place that shelters someone from danger or trouble, closer to the oasis metaphor than to its geography.
entries.definitionCN: 使人免受危险或困扰的庇护处，更接近绿洲的比喻而非地理义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real plurals, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复数形式、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One oasis, two oases: the Greek plural keeps -es, unlike the English -s.
normal.cn: 一个 oasis，两个 oases：希腊式复数保留 -es，而非英语的 -s。

normal.en: Oasis is green surrounded by dry: the word is built on contrast.
normal.cn: 绿洲是被干旱包围的绿：这个词建立在对比之上。

normal.en: An oasis has three parts: water, palms and people.
normal.cn: 绿洲有三部分：水、棕榈与人。

normal.en: An oasis of calm and an oasis of good news use the same contrast, with no sand.
normal.cn: 「宁静绿洲」与「好消息绿洲」用的是同一种对比，只是没有沙。

normal.en: In hydrology an oasis marks where an aquifer meets the surface.
normal.cn: 在水文学中，绿洲标记含水层与地表相接之处。

abstract.en: An oasis is a small argument against the desert.
abstract.cn: 绿洲是对沙漠的一个小小反驳。

abstract.en: Every long journey needs one oasis, even if it is only a hour of sleep.
abstract.cn: 每段长途都需要一片绿洲，哪怕只是一小时睡眠。

abstract.en: Kindness in a harsh week is an oasis: small, watered, and remembered.
abstract.cn: 艰难一周里的善意就是绿洲：不大、有水，且被记住。

examples.en: The oasis supports date palms and a small village.
examples.cn: 这片绿洲供养着枣椰树和一个小村庄。

examples.en: They found an oasis after three days in the desert.
examples.cn: 在沙漠里走了三天后，他们找到一片绿洲。

examples.en: The reading room was an oasis of quiet.
examples.cn: 阅览室是一片安静的绿洲。

dict_mnemonic.text: oasis＝沙漠里的一小片水与绿；复数 oases 用希腊式；引申为「纷扰中的安宁」与「困境中的慰藉」。

root: 经拉丁 oasis 与希腊 oasis 上溯埃及语中指沙漠水源地的词（可能为科普特语 ouahe）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of oasis. Water in dry land generates the spring, the settlement, the farming, the ecosystem, the hydrological origin, and then two metaphors of relief.
sensesIntro.cn: oasis 的八个义项。干旱之地中的水衍生出泉源、聚落、农业、生态系统与水文成因，再衍生出两种「宽慰」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small green circle of palms and water in the middle of yellow sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：黄沙中央一小圈棕榈与水的绿色。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND ITS WATER: the green spot, then the spring that makes it.
branches.cn: 地点与水：先是绿色地点，再是造就它的泉。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CROPS: the settlement built there, then the farming it supports.
branches.cn: 人与作物：先是在那里建起的聚落，再是它支撑的农业。

branches.en: THE ECOSYSTEM: an isolated community of plants and animals.
branches.cn: 生态系统：孤立的动植物群落。

branches.en: TWO METAPHORS OF RELIEF: calm inside noise, and good news inside failure.
branches.cn: 两种宽慰隐喻：喧闹中的安宁，失败中的好消息。

branches.en: THE HYDROLOGICAL ORIGIN: how water reaches the surface at all.
branches.cn: 水文成因：水究竟如何到达地表。

intro.en: Oasis is a borrowed noun with no English affix; its plural oases is the Greek pattern, and its productive life is in compounds such as oasis town.
intro.cn: oasis 是借入名词，不带英语词缀；复数 oases 是希腊式变化，它的构词活力体现在 oasis town 这类复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin oasis is itself a borrowing from Greek, which took it from Egyptian; there is no Latin root family to trace. Latin aqua and fons mean water and spring but are unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 oasis 本身借自希腊语，希腊语又借自埃及语，因此没有可追溯的拉丁词根词族。拉丁 aqua 与 fons 意为水与泉，但并不同源。

items.meaning: a watered place in a desert
items.example: The oasis lies halfway across the sand.
items.exampleCN: 绿洲位于沙海的中途。

items.example: Three oases dot the route.

intro.en: Dependency is depend plus -ency; depend comes from Latin dependere, de- plus pendere, to hang down from.
intro.cn: dependency 由 depend 加 -ency 构成；depend 源自拉丁语 dependere，由 de- 加 pendere（悬挂）构成：从…垂下来。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down from.
items.cn: dependere 意为从…垂下。

items.en: Depend entered English for relying on.
items.cn: 十五世纪 depend 以依靠义进入英语。

items.en: Dependency named the state of hanging on another.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dependency 指依附于他者的状态。

items.en: It came to name a territory ruled from abroad.
items.cn: 十八世纪转而指受外国统治的属地。

items.en: It named a software component another needs.
items.cn: 二十世纪指另一程序所需的软件组件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pend- hanging family; the near-meaning group names other things one leans on.

dict_mnemonic.text: dependency ＝ depend（依靠）＋ -ency（名词，状态）＝挂着别人的状态。depend 源自拉丁 de-（向下）＋ pendere（悬挂）：从别人身上垂下来，就是「依赖」。

root: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂）→ dependere（从…垂下）→ depend（依靠）＋ -ency → dependency
